<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CORPORATE STRUCTURE</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group is the holding company parent corporation of two principal, wholly owned subsidiaries, Central Hudson and CHEC.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson is a regulated electric and natural gas subsidiary.&#160;&#160;CHEC, the parent company of CH Energy Group&#8217;s unregulated businesses and investments, has six wholly owned subsidiaries, Griffith Energy Service, Inc. (&#8220;Griffith&#8221;), CH-Auburn Energy, LLC (&#8220;CH-Auburn&#8221;), CH-Greentree, LLC (&#8220;CH-Greentree&#8221;), CH-Lyonsdale, LLC (&#8220;CH-Lyonsdale&#8221;), Lyonsdale Biomass, LLC (&#8220;Lyonsdale&#8221;) and CH Shirley Wind, LLC (&#8220;CH Shirley&#8221;).&#160;&#160;CHEC also has ownership interests in certain subsidiaries that are less than 100%.&#160;&#160;For more information, see sub-caption &#8220;CHEC and Its Subsidiaries and Investments&#8221; under caption &#8220;Subsidiaries of CH Energy Group.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 45pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For a discussion of CH Energy Group&#8217;s and its subsidiaries&#8217; capital structure and financing program, see Item&#160;7 - &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221; of this 10-K Annual Report under the sub-captions &#8220;Capital Structure&#8221; and &#8220;Financing Program&#8221; under the caption &#8220;Capital Resources and Liquidity.&#8221;&#160;&#160;For a discussion of short-term borrowing, capitalization, and long-term debt, see Note&#160;7 - &#8220;Short-Term Borrowing Arrangements,&#8221; Note&#160;8 - &#8220;Capitalization - Common and Preferred Stock,&#8221; and Note&#160;9 - &#8220;Capitalization - Long-Term Debt,&#8221; respectively, to the financial statements contained in Item 8 - &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#8221; of this 10-K Annual Report (each Note being hereinafter called a &#8220;Note&#8221;).&#160;&#160;For information concerning revenues, certain expenses, earnings per share, and information regarding assets of Central Hudson&#8217;s regulated electric and regulated natural gas segments and of Griffith, see Note 13 - &#8220;Segments and Related Information.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">HOLDING COMPANY REGULATION</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group is a &#8220;holding company&#8221; under Public Utility Holding Company Act of 2005 (&#8220;PUHCA 2005&#8221;) because of its ownership interests in Central Hudson and CHEC. CH Energy Group, however, is exempt from regulation as a holding company under PUHCA 2005, because it derives substantially all of its public utility company revenues from business conducted within a single state, the State of New York.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group will retain this exemption until such time as it derives more than 13% of its public utility revenues from businesses conducted outside of the State of New York.&#160;&#160;At the present time, CH Energy Group cannot predict whether and when its circumstances may change such that it no longer qualifies for exemption from PUHCA 2005 or whether regulation under PUHCA 2005 would have a material impact on its financial condition or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">SUBSIDIARIES OF CH ENERGY GROUP</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Central Hudson</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is a New York State natural gas and electric corporation formed in 1926.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson purchases, sells at wholesale, and distributes electricity and natural gas at retail in portions of New York State.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson also generates a small portion of its electricity requirements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson serves a territory extending about 85 miles along the Hudson River and about 25 to 40 miles east and west of the Hudson River.&#160;&#160;The southern end of the territory is about 25 miles north of New York City and the northern end is about 10 miles south of the City of Albany.&#160;&#160;The territory, comprising approximately 2,600 square miles, has a population estimated at 688,000.&#160;&#160;Electric service is available throughout the territory, and natural gas service is provided in and about the cities of Poughkeepsie, Beacon, Newburgh, and Kingston, New York, and in certain outlying and intervening territories.&#160;&#160;The number of Central Hudson employees at December 31, 2010, was 856.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s territory reflects a diversified economy, including manufacturing industries, research firms, farms, governmental agencies, public and private institutions, resorts, and wholesale and retail trade operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Seasonality</font></div>
</div>

<div align="center">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s delivery revenues have historically varied seasonally in response to weather.&#160;&#160;Sales of electricity are usually highest during the summer months, primarily due to the use of air-conditioning and other cooling equipment.&#160;&#160;Sales of natural gas are highest during the winter months, primarily due to space heating usage.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s rates are developed based on forecasts of monthly sales volumes, which reflect natural seasonality under normal weather conditions.&#160;&#160;Effective July 1, 2009 and continuing in the 2010 Rate Order through June 30, 2013, Central Hudson&#8217;s delivery rate structure includes revenue decoupling mechanisms (&#8220;RDMs&#8221;), which provide the ability to record revenues equal to those forecasted in the development of current rates for most of Central Hudson&#8217;s customers.&#160;&#160;As a result, fluctuations in actual sales volumes as compared to those under normal weather conditions, no longer have a significant impact on earnings.&#160;&#160;However, higher expenses incurred due to storm activity than the amount set in rates may impact the Company&#8217;s earnings.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson has the ability to request regulatory recovery of significant incremental costs incurred if certain criteria are met as defined by the PSC and, as such, any impact on earnings for higher storm expenses should be limited to non-material amounts, as long as the other criteria for deferred accounting were met.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</font></div>
</div>

<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is a regulated utility with a legal obligation to deliver electricity and natural gas within its PSC-approved franchise territory.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson has no direct competitors in its electricity distribution business; indirect competitors include distributed generation systems, including net metered systems.&#160;&#160;To date, the primary source of competition is solar net metered systems, which are currently capped at 12 MW.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson was authorized by the PSC to defer lost revenues attributable to photovoltaic net metering through June 30, 2009, under an order issued in Case 07-E-0437 on October 19, 2007.&#160;&#160;Beginning July 1, 2009, Central Hudson no longer has the authorization to defer lost revenues attributable to photovoltaic net metering since the RDM provides similar protection.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s natural gas business competes with other fuels, especially fuel oil and propane.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The competitive marketplace continues to develop for electric and natural gas supply markets, and Central Hudson&#8217;s electric and natural gas customers may purchase energy and related services from other providers.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s rate making structure neutralizes any earnings impact of customers&#8217; decisions to purchase electricity and natural gas from other providers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation</font></div>

<div align="left">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is subject to regulation by the PSC regarding, among other things, services rendered (including the rates charged), major transmission facility siting, accounting treatment of certain items, and issuance of securities.&#160;&#160;For certain restrictions imposed by the Settlement Agreement, see Note&#160;2 - &#8220;Regulatory Matters.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Certain activities of Central Hudson, including accounting and the acquisition and disposition of property, are subject to regulation by FERC under the Federal Power Act.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is not subject to the provisions of the Natural Gas Act.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s hydroelectric facilities are not required to be licensed under the Federal Power Act but are regulated by the DEC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is subject to regulation by the North American Electric Reliability Corporation regarding its ownership, operation and use of bulk power system.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Rates</font></div>

<div align="left">&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">General</font>: The electric and natural gas rates charged by Central Hudson applicable to service supplied to retail customers within New York State are regulated by the PSC.&#160;&#160;Costs of service, both for electric and gas delivery service and for electric and gas supply costs, are recovered from customers through PSC approved tariffs, subject to a standard of prudency.&#160;&#160;Both transmission rates and rates for electricity sold for resale which involve&#160;interstate commerce&#160;are regulated by FERC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 2009 Rate Order provides for implementation of both Electric and Gas RDMs.&#160;&#160;RDMs are intended to minimize the earnings impact resulting from reduced energy consumption as energy efficiency programs are implemented by breaking the link between energy sales and utility revenues and/or profits.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s RDMs allow the Company to recognize electric delivery revenues and gas sales per customer at the levels approved in rates for most of Central Hudson&#8217;s electric and gas customer classes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s retail electricity rate structure consists of various service classifications covering delivery service and full service (which includes electricity supply) for residential, commercial, and industrial customers.&#160;&#160;Retail rates for delivery and supply are shown separately on retail bills to allow customers to see the costs associated with their commodity supply, and thus facilitate retail competition.&#160;&#160;During 2010, the average price of electricity for full service customers was 14.94 cents per kWh as compared to an average of 14.20 cents per kWh in 2009.&#160;&#160;The PSC has authorized Central Hudson to recover the costs of the electric commodity from customers, without earning a profit on the commodity costs.&#160;&#160;The average delivery price in 2010 was 5.26 cents per kWh and 4.44 cents per kWh in 2009.&#160;&#160;The increase in delivery price was primarily due to the implementation of new rates as part of the 2009 Rate Order and the 2010 Rate Order.&#160;&#160;The year over year increase related to the Rate Orders was approximately 0.51 cents per kWh.&#160;&#160;The additional increase is associated with updated surcharges to cover additional assessments from New York State agencies.&#160;&#160;The average delivery price in 2010 includes a surcharge of approximately 0.07 cents per kWh resulting from the Electric RDM.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s retail natural gas rate structure consists of various service classifications covering transport, retail access service, and full service (which includes natural gas supply) for residential, commercial, and industrial customers.&#160;&#160;During 2010, the average price of natural gas for full-service customers was $14.86 per Mcf as compared to an average of $15.83 per Mcf in 2009.&#160;&#160;The PSC has authorized Central Hudson to recover the costs of the gas commodity from customers, without earning a profit on the commodity costs.&#160;&#160;The average delivery price for natural gas for retail and full service in 2010 was $6.67 per Mcf and $5.14 per Mcf in 2009. The increase in delivery price was primarily due to the implementation of new rates as part of the 2009 Rate Order and the 2010 Rate Order.&#160;&#160;The average delivery price in 2010 includes a surcharge of approximately $0.05 per Mcf resulting from the Gas RDM.&#160;&#160;The increase in the average delivery price was more than offset by the decrease in gas commodity costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For further information regarding the terms of the 2006 Rate Order, 2009 Rate Order and 2010 Rate Order under which Central Hudson operated during the current reporting period, see Note 2 - &#8220;Regulatory Matters&#8221; under the captions &#8220;2006 Rate Order&#8221;, &#8220;2009 Rate Order&#8221; and &#8220;2010 Rate Order.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Cost Adjustment Clauses and RDMs</font>:&#160;&#160;For information regarding Central Hudson&#8217;s electric and natural gas cost adjustment clauses and RDMs, see Note&#160;1 - &#8220;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; under the caption &#8220;Rates, Revenues and Cost Adjustment Clauses.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is engaged in the conduct and support of research and development (&#8220;R&amp;D&#8221;) activities, which are focused on the improvement of existing energy technologies and the development of new technologies, including renewable energy sources, for the delivery and use of energy.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s R&amp;D expenditures were $3.1 million in 2010 and $3.9 million in both 2009 and 2008.&#160;&#160;These expenditures were for internal research programs and for contributions to research administered by NYSERDA, the Electric Power Research Institute, and other industry organizations.&#160;&#160;Recovery of expenditures for R&amp;D is provided for in Central Hudson&#8217;s rates charged to customers for electric and natural gas delivery service with any differences between R&amp;D expense and the rate allowances deferred for future recovery from or return to customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Central Hudson Matters</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Labor Relations</font>:&#160;&#160;Central Hudson has an agreement with Local&#160;320 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers for its approximate 533 unionized employees, representing construction and maintenance employees, customer service representatives, service workers, and clerical employees (excluding persons in managerial, professional, or supervisory positions).&#160;&#160;This agreement became effective on May&#160;1, 2008, and remains effective through April&#160;30, 2011.&#160;&#160;It provided for an average annual general wage increase of 4.0% and changes to fringe benefits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CHEC and Its Subsidiaries and Investments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CHEC, a New York corporation, is a wholly owned subsidiary of CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;Through its subsidiaries and investments, CHEC&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiary Griffith is engaged in the business of marketing petroleum products and related services to retail and wholesale customers.&#160;&#160;CHEC also provides service and maintenance of energy conservation measures and generation systems for private businesses, institutions, and government entities.&#160;&#160;CHEC also participates in cogeneration, wind generation, biomass energy projects, landfill gas projects and alternate fuel and energy production projects in New Jersey, New Hampshire, New York, Wisconsin and Pennsylvania, and a corn-ethanol plant in Nebraska.&#160;&#160;For further discussion of certain energy-related projects within other subsidiaries and investments, see Note 5 - &#8220;Acquisitions, Divestitures and Investments.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Griffith</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Griffith is an energy services company engaged in fuel distribution, including heating oil, gasoline, diesel fuel, kerosene, and propane, and the installation and maintenance of heating, ventilating, and air conditioning equipment.&#160;&#160;During most of 2009, Griffith operated in Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New York, New Jersey and Washington, D.C.&#160;&#160;On December 11, 2009, Griffith closed on the sale of operations within certain geographic locations, which included approximately 45,000 customers in Rhode Island, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and New York.&#160;&#160;Since being acquired by CHEC in November 2000, Griffith acquired the assets of 45 regional fuel oil, propane, and related services companies.&#160;&#160;Of these acquisitions, 20 remain with Griffith following the 2009 divestiture.&#160;&#160;The number of Griffith employees at December 31, 2010 was 394.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CHEC and Griffith participate in competitive industries that are subject to different risks than those found in the businesses of the regulated utility, Central Hudson.&#160;&#160;As a competitor in the unregulated fuel distribution business, Griffith faces competition from other fuel distribution companies and from companies supplying other fuels for heating, such as natural gas and propane.&#160;&#160;For a discussion of Griffith&#8217;s operating revenues and operating income, see the caption &#8220;Results of Operations&#8221; in Item&#160;7 - &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221; of this 10-K Annual Report.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY REGULATION</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson, Griffith, CH&#8722;Auburn, Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind are subject to regulation by federal, state, and local authorities with respect to the environmental effects of their operations. Environmental matters may expose Central Hudson, Griffith, CH&#8722;Auburn, Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind to potential liability, which, in certain instances, may be imposed without regard to fault or may be premised on historical activities that were lawful at the time they occurred.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson, Griffith, CH&#8722;Auburn, Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind each monitor their activities in order to determine their impact on the environment and to comply with applicable environmental laws and regulations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The principal environmental areas relevant to these companies (air, water and industrial and hazardous wastes, other) are described below. Unless otherwise noted, all required permits and certifications have been obtained by the applicable company. Management believes that each company was in material compliance with these permits and certifications during 2010, except as noted in &#8220;Note 12 &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies&#8221; under the caption &#8220;Environmental Matters&#8221; of this 10-K Annual Report.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Air Quality</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Clean Air Act Amendments of 1990 address attainment and maintenance of national air quality standards, including control of particulate emissions from fossil&#8722;fueled electric generating plants and emissions that affect &#8220;acid rain&#8221; and ozone. The impacted facilities are the Central Hudson South Cairo and Coxsackie, NY electric generating facilities, Lyonsdale&#8217;s electric generating plant and CH-Auburn. See Note12 &#8722; &#8220;Commitments and Contingencies&#8221; under the caption &#8220;Environmental Matters&#8221; regarding the investigation by the EPA into the compliance of a former major Central Hudson generating asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH-Auburn has received a Notice of Violation of its air permit from the NYS DEC.&#160;&#160;CH-Auburn is currently working with the NYS DEC to resolve this issue.&#160;&#160;While resolving the issue, CH-Auburn will not run one of its three engine generators, but continues to meet its obligations under the Energy Services Agreement with the City of Auburn.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Water Quality</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Clean Water Act established the basic framework for federal and state regulation of water pollution control and requires facilities that discharge waste or storm water into the waters of the United States to obtain permits. Central Hudson, Griffith and Lyonsdale have permits regulating pollutant discharges for relevant locations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Industrial &amp; Hazardous Substances and Wastes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson, Griffith, CH&#8722;Auburn, Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind are subject to federal, state and local laws and regulations relating to the use, handling, storage, treatment, transportation, and disposal of industrial, hazardous, and toxic wastes. Currently, there are no permit or certification requirements for Griffith, CH&#8722;Auburn, </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Lyonsdale and/or Shirley Wind. See Note 12 &#8722; &#8220;Commitments and Contingencies&#8221; under the caption &#8220;Environmental Matters&#8221; for additional discussion regarding, among other things, Central Hudson&#8217;s former MGP facilities and Little Britain Road.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 108pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ITEM1A">ITEM 1A</a> - Risk Factors</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CENTRAL HUDSON&#8217;S RATES LIMIT ITS ABILITY TO RECOVER ITS COSTS FROM ITS CUSTOMERS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Description and Sources of Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s retail rates are regulated by the PSC.&#160;&#160;Rates generally may not be changed during their respective terms.&#160;&#160;Therefore, rates cannot be modified for higher expenses than those assumed in the current rates, absent circumstances such as an increase in expenses that meet the PSC&#8217;s threshold requirements for filing for approval of deferral accounting.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson is operating under a three year rate order plan approved by the PSC effective July 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;The following could unfavorably impact Central Hudson&#8217;s financial results:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Higher expenses than reflected in current rates.&#160;&#160;Higher expenses could result from, among other things, increases in taxes and assessments, storm restoration expense, labor, health care benefits or other expense components.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">UNUSUAL TEMPERATURES IN GRIFFITH&#8217;S SERVICE TERRITORIES MAY ADVERSELY IMPACT EARNINGS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Description and Sources of Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Griffith serves the Mid-Atlantic region of the United States.&#160;&#160;This area experiences seasonal fluctuations in temperature.&#160;&#160;A considerable portion of Griffith&#8217;s earnings is derived directly or indirectly from the weather-sensitive end uses of space heating and air conditioning.&#160;&#160;As a result, sales volumes fluctuate and vary from normal expected levels based on variations in weather from historically normal seasonal levels.&#160;&#160;Such variations could significantly reduce sales volumes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Potential Impacts</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Griffith could experience lower delivery volumes in periods of milder than normal weather, leading to lower earnings and reduced cash flows.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">GRIFFITH&#8217;S ABILITY TO ATTRACT NEW CUSTOMERS, RETAIN EXISTING CUSTOMERS, MAINTAIN SALES VOLUMES, AND MAINTAIN MARGINS MAY ADVERSELY IMPACT EARNINGS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Description and Sources of Risk</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Lower sales can occur for various reasons, including the following:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Changes in customers&#8217; usage patterns driven by customer responses to product prices.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div>

</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

</div>

<table align="center" border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="hangingindent" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson owns substations having an aggregate transformer capacity of 5.0 million kilovolt amperes.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s electric transmission system consists of 629 pole miles of line.&#160;&#160;The electric distribution system consists of over 8,200 pole miles of overhead lines and over 1,400 trench miles of underground lines, as well as customer service lines and meters.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Electric Load and Capacity</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s maximum one-hour demand for electricity within its own territory for the year ended December 31, 2010, occurred on July 6, 2010, and amounted to 1,229 MW.&#160;&#160;In prior summer periods peak electric demand has reached 1,295 MW which occurred on August 2, 2006.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s maximum one-hour demand for electricity within its own territory for that part of the 2010-2011 winter capability period through January&#160;18, 2011, occurred on December 14, 2010, and amounted to 891 MW.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson owns minimal generating capacity and relies on purchased capacity and energy from third-party providers to meet the demands of its full service customers.&#160;&#160;For more information, see Note&#160;12 - &#8220;Commitments and Contingencies.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural Gas</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s natural gas system consists of 164 miles of transmission pipelines and 1,176 miles of distribution pipelines, as well as customer service lines and meters.&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2010, the total amount of natural gas purchased by Central Hudson from all sources was 11,793,624 Mcf.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson owns two propane-air mixing facilities for emergency and peak-shaving purposes, one located in Poughkeepsie, New York, and the other in Newburgh, New York.&#160;&#160;These facilities, in aggregate, are capable of supplying 8,000 Mcf per day with propane storage capability adequate to provide maximum facility output for up to six consecutive days.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The peak daily demand for natural gas of Central Hudson&#8217;s customers for the year ended December 31, 2010, and for that part of the 2010-2011 heating season through January&#160;30, 2011, occurred on January 23, 2011, and amounted to 114,599 Mcf.&#160;&#160;In prior years, winter period daily peak demand has reached 125,496 Mcf which occurred on January 27, 2005.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s firm peak day natural gas capability in the 2010-2011 heating season was 142,992 Mcf, which excludes approximately 5,000 Mcf of transport customer deliveries.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson owns its corporate headquarters, which is located in Poughkeepsie, New York.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s electric generating plants and important property units are generally held by it in fee simple, except for certain ROW and a portion of the property used in connection with hydroelectric plants consisting of flowage or other riparian rights.&#160;&#160;Certain of the Central Hudson properties are subject to ROW and easements that do not interfere with Central Hudson&#8217;s operations.&#160;&#160;In the case of certain distribution lines, Central Hudson owns only a partial interest in the poles upon which its wires are installed and the remaining interest is owned by various telecommunications companies.&#160;&#160;In addition, certain electric and natural gas transmission facilities owned by others are used by Central Hudson under long-term contracts.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the three-year period ended December 31, 2010, Central Hudson made gross property additions of $243.5 million and property retirements and adjustments of $38.7 million, resulting in a net increase (including construction work in progress) in gross utility plant of $204.8 million, or 16%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2010, CH Energy Group maintained its quarterly dividend rate at $0.54 per share.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s strategy targets stable and predictable earnings, with growth trend expectations of 5% or more per year off a base of $2.76 in 2009.&#160;&#160;If this trend of earnings per share growth is achieved and sustainable, it should facilitate increases in CH Energy Group&#8217;s annual dividend rate, subject to maintaining a target payout ratio in the range of 65% to 70%.&#160;&#160;In making future dividend decisions, CH Energy Group will evaluate all circumstances at the time of making such decisions, including business, financial, and regulatory considerations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s ability to pay dividends is affected by the ability of its subsidiaries to pay dividends.&#160;&#160;The Federal Power Act limits the payment of dividends by Central Hudson to its retained earnings.&#160;&#160;More restrictive is the PSC&#8217;s limit on the dividends Central Hudson may pay to CH Energy Group which is 100% of the average annual income available for common stock, calculated on a two-year rolling average basis.&#160;&#160;Based on this calculation as of December 31, 2010, Central Hudson would be able to pay a maximum of $38.5 million in dividends to CH Energy Group without violating the restrictions by the PSC.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s dividend would be reduced to 75% of its average annual income in the event of a downgrade of its senior debt rating below &#8220;BBB+&#8221; by more than one rating agency if the stated reason for the downgrade is related to CH Energy Group or any of Central Hudson&#8217;s affiliates.&#160;&#160;Further restrictions are imposed for any downgrades below this level.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2010, Central Hudson declared and paid dividends of $31.0 million to CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s other subsidiaries do not have express restrictions on their ability to pay dividends.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The number of registered holders of Common Stock of CH Energy Group as of December 31, 2010 was 14,472.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All of the outstanding Common Stock of Central Hudson and all of the outstanding Common Stock of CHEC are held by CH Energy Group.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s objective is to deliver value to its shareholders through current income, in the form of quarterly dividend payments, and through share price appreciation that is expected to result from earnings growth over the long term.&#160;&#160;In 2010, Management completed an update to its strategic plan.&#160;&#160;The updated plan reflects a shift in our strategy that we believe will achieve greater shareholder value with less risk.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group has determined that its greatest strengths are in the operation and growth of its energy distribution businesses, and henceforth it will focus its time and resources on Central Hudson and Griffith.&#160;&#160;Business development efforts in renewable energy have been discontinued and CH Energy Group is&#160;evaluating options&#160;to divest existing renewable energy investments in a manner that maximizes shareholder value.&#160;&#160;This shift in corporate strategy is further described below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s mission is to provide electricity, natural gas, petroleum and related services to an expanding customer base in a safe, reliable, courteous and affordable manner; to produce growing financial returns for shareholders; to foster a culture that encourages employees to reach their full potential; and to be a good corporate citizen.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s strategy is to provide an attractive risk adjusted return to its shareholders by investing primarily in Central Hudson&#8217;s utility transmission and distribution systems while maintaining a strong focus on risk management, including limiting commodity risk, effectively managing regulatory affairs, and maintaining a strong financial profile.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group also intends to increase earnings by expanding Griffith&#8217;s service offerings and customer base while maintaining strong cost controls.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s strategy targets stable and predictable earnings, with growth trend expectations of 5% or more per year off a base of $2.76 in 2009.&#160;&#160;If this trend of earnings per share growth is achieved and sustainable, it should facilitate increases in CH Energy Group&#8217;s annual dividend rate, subject to maintaining a target payout ratio in the range of 65% to 70%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Central Hudson</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s earnings are derived primarily from the revenue it generates from delivering energy to approximately 300,000 electric customers and 75,000 natural gas customers.&#160;&#160;The delivery rates Central Hudson charges its customers are set by the PSC and are designed to recover the cost of providing safe and reliable service to Central Hudson&#8217;s customers while providing the opportunity to earn a fair and reasonable return on the capital invested by shareholders.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson has strong competencies in safe and efficient utility operations, financial management, risk management and regulatory affairs which will facilitate the achievement of its strategy.&#160;&#160;In 2010, Central Hudson expanded its current cost management and innovation programs by launching a company-wide initiative utilizing Lean Six Sigma techniques, which is a data driven approach to improving business processes, reducing cost, and improving service quality.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the second half of 2009 and throughout 2010, Central Hudson continued to demonstrate improved financial results under rate orders that better align revenue recovery with operating costs and capital expenditure levels.&#160;&#160;The current three-year rate plan, which commenced on July 1, 2010, is expected to reduce uncertainty and risk and support investment in Central Hudson&#8217;s infrastructure to improve the quality of service to customers.&#160;&#160;Management believes this rate plan demonstrates a constructive relationship with New York State regulators and the willingness of regulators to enable Central Hudson to earn stable, predictable returns while providing reliable, high quality service and fulfilling state energy policy objectives.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Earnings growth is primarily expected to come from increases in utility plant reflected in rate base and also in part from effective cost management.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson invests significant capital on an annual basis to attach new customers to our system and to replace aging infrastructure and to maintain and improve service quality and reliability.&#160;&#160;Over the long term, increased investment levels to expand Central Hudson's&#160;natural gas and electric transmission are also possible.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The key risks Management sees in achieving this strategy are the regulatory environment, cost management and the economy in Central Hudson&#8217;s service territory.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s ability to meet its financial objectives is largely dependent on the consistency of the PSC ratemaking practices.&#160;&#160;Risks related to these practices include reduced allowed returns on equity and/or reduced probabilities of achieving allowed returns, an inability to recover the costs of doing business, declining support for strong capital structures and credit ratings, changes in deferral accounting that increase volatility of earnings and/or defer cash recovery of our costs, elimination of RDMs and changes in the mechanisms currently in place for recovery of our commodity purchases.&#160;&#160;Additionally, lower interest rates could lead to a decrease in the authorized ROE in a future rate proceeding.&#160;&#160;Management believes Central Hudson&#8217;s commitments to providing safe and reliable service, customer satisfaction, operational excellence and promoting positive customer and regulatory relations are important for supportive regulatory relationships and obtaining full cost recovery and competitive returns for shareholders.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The third risk &#8211; the economy in Central Hudson&#8217;s service territory affects the ability to collect receivables and the growth of utility rate base and earnings through a direct relationship to customer additions and peak demand growth.&#160;&#160;Management believes the economy in Central Hudson&#8217;s service territory has good long-term growth prospects, but unexpected prolonged downturns could inhibit its ability to meet long term business objectives.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Additional information regarding the 2010 Rate Order is discussed within the &#8220;Regulatory Matters &#8211; PSC Proceedings&#8221; section.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Griffith</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2010, Management resumed seeking selective &#8220;tuck-in&#8221; acquisitions, which are expected to be funded from internally generated cash.&#160;&#160;This growth strategy focuses on acquiring and retaining customers in geographic areas that overlap Griffith&#8217;s existing operations.&#160;&#160;Griffith acquired one fuel distribution and service company in 2010 and acquired two additional companies subsequent to year-end.&#160;&#160;Management expects to generate additional earnings and cash flow as a result of the expansion of its HVAC business.&#160;&#160;These growth strategies are not expected to result in the growth of CH Energy Group&#8217;s total invested capital in Griffith.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management sees two key risks associated with this strategy.&#160;&#160;The primary factor that could prevent Griffith from achieving earnings growth is a sustained, significant increase in wholesale oil prices, which could reduce residential sales volumes, put downward pressure on margins and increase bad debt expense.&#160;&#160;While Management believes that margin expansion would still be possible in this environment as competitors would be forced to increase their prices to cover their costs, Management expects that this result would lag the increase in commodity prices.&#160;&#160;Secondarily, weakness in the economy of the Mid-Atlantic region could limit Griffith&#8217;s ability to expand margins since customers&#8217; willingness and ability to pay are typically tied to income levels and unemployment rates.&#160;&#160;Management believes that the economy in Griffith&#8217;s service territory is relatively strong and stable with a large pool of current and prospective customers that value quality service at a fair price, and is thereby supportive of Griffith&#8217;s strategy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Businesses and Investments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As noted earlier, CH Energy Group has decided to discontinue investing in the renewable energy industry through CHEC for the following reasons:</font></div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 63pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">-&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management believes that CH Energy Group lacks competitive advantage and sufficiently strong internal core competencies in this market;</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">

</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management&#8217;s experience in this market indicates that it is difficult to earn an appropriate rate of return without employing higher debt leverage than is consistent with CH Energy Group&#8217;s credit quality objectives; and</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The earnings profile of renewable energy projects does not support CH Energy Group&#8217;s current strategy and near term financial objective to increase the dividend because the returns typically start low and increases over time.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group has evaluated CHEC&#8217;s current renewable energy investments and has initiated plans to actively market some of these investments, specifically Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind.&#160;&#160;Management will continue to evaluate the market for the remaining investments in 2011.&#160;&#160;With regard to biomass investments, Management does not believe such assets possess earnings and cash flow characteristics that are consistent with the updated strategy and is seeking to sell the assets in the near term.&#160;&#160;With regard to CHEC&#8217;s investment in wind and landfill gas energy, Management feels that these investments reflect acceptable earnings and cash flow characteristics, however Management has determined it will no longer seek to build a business in these areas as they are no longer aligned with the Company&#8217;s strategy.&#160;&#160;Management believes greater shareholder value can be created by opportunistically divesting these assets.&#160;&#160;However, if attractive terms of sale are not available in the near-term, holding existing investments in wind and landfill gas is not expected to require significant management oversight or further capital investment.&#160;&#160;Proceeds from the sale of any of these investments are expected to be used primarily for the repurchase of common stock and repayment of debt associated with these assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following discussion and analyses include explanations of significant changes in revenues and expenses between the year ended December 31, 2010, and 2009, and the year ended December 31, 2009, and 2008 for Central Hudson&#8217;s regulated electric and natural gas businesses, Griffith, and the Other Businesses and Investments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The discussions and tables below present the change in earnings of CH Energy Group&#8217;s business units in terms of earnings for each share of CH Energy Group&#8217;s Common Stock.&#160;&#160;Management believes that expressing the results in terms of the impact on shares of CH Energy Group is useful to investors because it shows the relative contribution of the various business units to CH Energy Group&#8217;s earnings.&#160;&#160;This information is considered a non-GAAP financial measure and not an alternative to earnings per share determined on a consolidated basis, which is the most directly comparable GAAP measure.&#160;&#160;Additionally, Management believes that the disclosure of Significant Events within each business unit provides investors with the context around the Company's results that is important in enabling them to ascertain the likelihood that past performance is indicative of future performance.&#160;&#160;A reconciliation of each business unit&#8217;s earnings per share to CH Energy Group&#8217;s earnings per share, determined on a consolidated basis, is included in the table below.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(1)</font></div>
</td>
<td align="left" colspan="10" valign="top" width="98%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Excludes incremental costs incurred associated with the severe storms that occurred in late February 2010, which have been deferred for future recovery from customers.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block">Earnings from Central Hudson's electric and natural gas operations increased in the year ended December 31, 2010 compared to 2009 primarily due to the increases in electric and natural gas delivery rates, including the RDM, which became effective July 1, 2009 and 2010.&#160;&#160;These increases provided revenues that better align with Central Hudson's costs of providing safe and reliable service to customers and provide an opportunity to earn an appropriate return for shareholders.&#160;&#160;Higher operating expenses partially offset the favorable impacts of delivery rate increases.&#160;&#160;The net increase in year-over-year results includes the impact of lower earnings during the first six months of 2009 resulting from the sales shortfall under the expiring 2006 Rate Order.</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block">Griffith&#8217;s earnings decreased for the year ended December 31, 2010 compared to the same period in 2009.&#160;&#160;This decrease was primarily attributable to the sale of operations in certain geographic locations at the end of 2009.&#160;&#160;The gain recorded as a result of the sale and the decreased customer base resulted in a decrease in 2010 earnings as compared to 2009.&#160;&#160;Unfavorable impacts of weather and continued customer conservation also contributed to the decreased earnings, but were offset by lower operating expenses resulting from cost reductions implemented by Management to align its cost structure to its smaller size following the partial divestiture.&#160;&#160;Lower uncollectible accounts also favorably impacted 2010's results.</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font size="2" style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The earnings activity of CH Energy Group (the holding company) and CHEC&#8217;s partnerships and other investments decreased in the year ended December 31, 2010 compared to the same period in 2009 primarily due to 2010 impairment charges for CHEC's ethanol and biomass investments.&#160;&#160;The expiration of production tax credits related to CHEC&#8217;s biomass investment on December 31, 2009 and a repair to the plant's steam turbine also negatively impacted earnings.&#160;&#160;CHEC's earnings from its ethanol investment were also lower in 2010 due&#160;to lower crush margins and lower prices for one of the byproducts of the production process.&#160;&#160;These decreases were partially reduced by a favorable change to the effective tax rate of the consolidated entity resulting in overall lower tax expense.&#160;&#160;The additional taxes in 2009 related to Griffith's partial divestiture.</font></font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt">Earnings from Central Hudson's electric and natural gas operations increased $0.35 per share in 2009 compared to 2008.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson's contribution to earnings per share was $2.02 per share, an increase of $0.35 per share over the $1.67 per share posted in 2008.&#160;&#160;The improvement is due primarily to improved cost recovery though delivery rates, though higher uncollectible accounts, depreciation, property taxes and other expenses offset much of the increased revenue.&#160;&#160;The absence of major storms and the resulting expense of restoring service to electric customers contributed $0.09 per share to year-over-year performance.

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt">Griffith&#8217;s earnings increased $0.50 per share in 2009 compared to 2008.&#160;&#160;Griffith contributed $0.76 to earnings per share in 2009 as compared to $0.26 per share in 2008.&#160;&#160;This increase was primarily attributable to the sale of operations in certain geographic locations.&#160;&#160;Customer conservation continued to have a negative impact on sales, but was offset by the favorable impacts of weather and continued operational cost reductions implemented by Management.</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Delivery Volumes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Delivery volumes for Central Hudson vary in response to weather conditions and customer behavior.&#160;&#160;Electric deliveries peak in the summer and deliveries of natural gas used for heating purposes peak in the winter.&#160;&#160;Delivery volumes also vary as customers respond to the price of the particular energy product and changes in local economic conditions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following chart reflects the change in the level of electric and natural gas deliveries for Central Hudson in 2010, compared to 2009, and in 2009, compared to 2008.&#160;&#160;Deliveries of electricity and natural gas to residential and commercial customers have historically contributed the most to Central Hudson's earnings.&#160;&#160;Industrial sales and interruptible sales have a negligible impact on earnings.&#160;&#160;Effective July 1, 2009 and continuing in the 2010 Rate Order, Central Hudson&#8217;s delivery rate structure includes a RDM which provides the ability to record revenues equal to those forecasted in the development of current rates for most of Central Hudson&#8217;s customers.&#160;&#160;As a result, fluctuations in actual delivery volumes no longer have a significant impact on Central Hudson&#8217;s earnings.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2010 vs. 2009</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Electric deliveries to residential and commercial customers increased during the year ended December 31, 2010 as compared to the prior year primarily as a result of the year-over-year impact of both the warmer than normal summer of 2010 and cooler than normal summer weather in 2009 partially offset by lower use per customer.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Natural gas deliveries to residential and commercial customers decreased during the year ended December 31, 2010 as compared to 2009 primarily as a result of unfavorable warmer than normal weather during the first quarter of 2010, despite a weather normalized increased use per customer during the year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The increase in natural gas industrial and other deliveries for the year ended December 31, 2010 as compared to the prior year was primarily driven by an increase in transportation delivery volumes to electric generation facilities, which sell their electricity to the NYISO market.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2009 vs. 2008</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Electric and natural gas deliveries to residential and commercial customers during 2009 were negatively impacted by declines in use per customer compared to the previous year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For electric deliveries, the cooler summer weather experienced in 2009 compared to 2008, further contributed to the decline in sales.&#160;&#160;Natural gas deliveries to residential and commercial customers in 2009 were favorably impacted by a slight increase in heating degree days, but were not enough to offset the lower use per customer.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenues</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s revenues consist of two major categories: those which offset specific expenses in the current period (matching revenues), and those that impact earnings.&#160;&#160;Matching revenues recover Central Hudson's actual costs for particular expenses.&#160;&#160;Any difference between these revenues and the actual expenses incurred is deferred for future recovery from or refund to customers and therefore does not impact earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>
