<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Electric revenues increased for the year ended December 31, 2010 as compared to the same period in 2009 primarily due to higher delivery rates and higher other revenues with matching offsets.&#160;&#160;These increases were reduced by a decrease in energy cost adjustment revenues as a result of lower purchased volumes and wholesale prices, as well as a decrease in revenues required to be recovered for previously deferred purchased electric costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Electric revenues decreased in the year ended December 31, 2009, as compared to the same period in 2008 primarily due to lower cost adjustment revenues.&#160;&#160;This resulted from both lower wholesale prices and lower delivery volumes.&#160;&#160;The decrease in electric cost adjustment revenues was partially offset by an increase in other revenues with matching offsets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Natural gas revenues decreased for the year ended December 31, 2010 as compared to the same period in 2009 primarily due to lower energy cost adjustment revenues partially reduced by higher delivery rates, higher other revenues with matching offsets and higher revenues related to regulatory revenue recovery mechanisms, primarily RDMs.&#160;&#160;Lower energy cost adjustment revenues resulted primarily from lower natural gas prices, as well as a decrease in purchased volume and revenues required to be recovered for previously deferred purchased natural gas costs.&#160;&#160;Lower revenues from gas sales to others for resale also contributed to the decrease in natural gas revenues.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Natural gas revenues decreased in the year ended December 31, 2009, as compared to the same period in 2008 primarily due to lower energy cost adjustment revenues.&#160;&#160;This was primarily driven by lower net gas costs.&#160;&#160;Lower revenues from gas sales to others for resale also contributed to the decrease in natural gas revenues.&#160;&#160;Decreased natural gas revenues were partially offset by an increase in other revenues with matching expense offsets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Higher revenues with matching offsets for both periods and for both electric and gas revenues were primarily driven by the Temporary State Assessment implemented in April 2009,&#160;an increase in rates related to increased pension costs and New York State (&#8220;NYS&#8221;) energy efficiency programs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Incentive Arrangements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under certain earnings incentive provisions approved by the PSC, Central Hudson shares with its customers certain revenues and/or cost savings exceeding predetermined levels or is penalized in some cases for shortfalls from certain performance standards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Earnings sharing arrangements are currently effective for interruptible natural gas deliveries and natural gas capacity release transactions.&#160;&#160;Performance standards apply to electric service reliability, certain aspects of customer service, natural gas safety, customer satisfaction, and certain aspects of retail market participant satisfaction.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The net results of these and previous earnings sharing arrangements had the effect of increasing pre-tax earnings by $0.5 million in 2010, $0.1 million in 2009, and $0.7 million in 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to the above-noted items, for the period from July 1, 2006 through June 30, 2009, Central Hudson was required to share with customers earnings over a base ROE of 10.6% on the equity portion of Central Hudson&#8217;s rate base, which was determined in accordance with the criteria set forth in the 2006 Rate Order.&#160;&#160;For the period from July 1, 2009 through June 30, 2010, Central Hudson was no longer required per the 2009 Rate Order to share earnings.&#160;&#160;Beginning July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2013, per the 2010 Rate Order, Central Hudson is once again required to share with customers earnings over a base ROE of 10.5% on the equity portion of Central Hudson&#8217;s rate base.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson did not record shared earnings in 2010, 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating Expenses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The most significant elements of Central Hudson&#8217;s operating expenses are purchased electricity and purchased natural gas; however, changes in these costs do not affect earnings since they are offset by changes in related revenues recovered through Central Hudson&#8217;s energy cost adjustment mechanisms.&#160;&#160;Additionally, there are other costs that are matched to revenues largely from customer billings, notably the cost of pensions and OPEBs, the new Temporary State Assessment, and NYS energy efficiency programs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Variations in pension, NYS energy programs, MGP site remediation and other matched expenses in 2010 are due to a change in the level of expenses recorded, with a corresponding change in revenues, incorporated in delivery rates as authorized in the 2009 and 2010 Rate Orders.&#160;&#160;In addition, a new Temporary State Assessment was instituted in April 2009 and effective July 1, 2009 collected from customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The increase in expenses currently matched to revenues from 2008 to 2009 is attributable to the increase in NYS energy program expenses&#160;related to the costs of energy efficiency programs under the Energy Efficiency Portfolio Standard, as well as, higher spending levels associated with other energy programs as authorized by both the 2009 and 2010 Rate Orders.&#160;&#160;Additional increases are due to the new Temporary State Assessment discussed above and an increase in pension costs incorporated in delivery rates in both the 2009 and 2010 Rate Orders.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Uncollectible expense decreased in the year ended December 31, 2010 as compared to the same period in 2009 primarily as a result of lower write-offs of customer receivables and a decrease in the amount recorded as a reserve for future uncollectible accounts.&#160;&#160;Management believes this is a result of enhanced collection efforts, including increased resources and improved planning.&#160;&#160;Additionally, in the second quarter of 2010, Central Hudson deferred an additional $1.1 million of gas uncollectible expense based on the authorization from the PSC covering the calendar year 2009 as compared to the requested and previously deferred amount related to the six months ended June 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson also deferred for future recovery $2.6 million in uncollectible electric expense over rate allowances for the rate year ended June 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;&#160;On September 23, 2010, Central Hudson filed a petition with the PSC for approval and recovery of the $2.6 million uncollectible electric expense.&#160;&#160;If the PSC does not approve the petition in full, Central Hudson&#8217;s expenses would increase by the amount of the petition denied by the PSC.&#160;&#160;Management believes the incremental expense meets the PSC criteria and is probable of future recovery.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Uncollectible expense increased in 2009, which Management believes is a result of the unfavorable economic conditions, particularly the rise in unemployment rates.&#160;&#160;The higher wholesale prices in 2008 also had an impact on customers&#8217; ability to pay their bills.&#160;&#160;Additionally, in 2009 Central Hudson deferred approximately $3.3 million of uncollectible expense and requested PSC authorization for future recovery from customers.&#160;&#160;The PSC approved this request in the second quarter of 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Storm restoration costs can fluctuate from year to year based on changes in the number and severity of storms each year.&#160;&#160;The higher storm restoration costs in 2010 were primarily the result of the most significant storm event in the Company&#8217;s history during the last week of February 2010.&#160;&#160;These costs do not include incremental costs from this major storm event, such as the costs of mutual aid crews and contractors from other areas and overtime costs for Central Hudson crews, which have been deferred for future recovery from customers.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson filed a petition with the PSC for approval and recovery on September 23, 2010.&#160;&#160;Management believes the incremental expense meets the PSC criteria and is probable of future recovery.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other income and deductions for Central Hudson for the year ended December 31, 2010, increased $0.8 million, compared to the same period in 2009, due to several factors, including an increase in regulatory carrying charges due from customers related to the Temporary State Assessment, February 2010 storm event and deferred uncollectible expense, as well as a regulatory adjustment resulting from changes in interest costs on Central Hudson&#8217;s variable rate long-term debt.&#160;&#160;These increases were partially offset by lower earnings on Deferred Compensation Plan assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other income and deductions for Central Hudson for the year ended December 31, 2009, decreased $2.1 million, compared to the same period in 2008, primarily due to a decrease in regulatory carrying charges due from customers related to pension costs and regulatory adjustments resulting from changes in interest costs on Central Hudson&#8217;s variable rate long-term debt.&#160;&#160;The latter adjustment offsets the decrease in interest on the variable rate debt, as discussed under the caption &#8220;Interest Charges.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The impact of these decreases on earnings was reduced by higher earnings on Deferred Compensation Plan assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Interest Charges</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s interest charges increased $1.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2010, compared to the same period in December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The increase is primarily the result of a medium-term note issuance of $24 million in October 2009 and<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>the issuance of $40 million of 2010 Series A and B notes in September of 2010.&#160;&#160;These debt issuances were partially offset by the redemption of $24 million of medium-term notes in September 2010.&#160;&#160;These issuances and redemptions resulted in a net increase in average debt outstanding during the year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s interest charges decreased $0.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2009, compared to the same period in 2008.&#160;&#160;Increases resulting from higher outstanding debt balances and increased carrying charges due customers were offset primarily by a decrease in interest rates on variable rate notes and short-term borrowings.&#160;&#160;Issuances of $30 million in medium-term notes in November 2008 and $24 million in October 2009, offset by the redemption of $20 million in January 2009, resulted in a net increase in average outstanding debt during the year.&#160;&#160;The increase in carrying charges due customers was primarily related to an increase in the underlying reserve balance for other post-retirement benefits and carrying charges beginning July 1, 2009 on the net regulatory electric liability set aside for future customer benefit.&#160;&#160;Lower working capital requirements as a result of decreasing energy prices allowed Central Hudson to decrease short-term borrowings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Sales of petroleum products decreased 39% in the year ended December 31, 2010 compared to the same period in 2009.&#160;&#160;The decrease was due primarily to the sale of operations in certain geographic locations.&#160;&#160;Excluding the impact of the partial divestiture, sales were lower primarily due to reduced sales to commercial customers that can burn both natural gas and oil due to the unfavorable price relationship between heating oil and natural gas.&#160;&#160;Additionally, sales of residential and commercial heating oil were lower due to weather that was 2% warmer in the twelve months ended December 31, 2010, compared to the same period in 2009, as measured by heating degree days.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating Expenses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the year ended December 31, 2010, operating expenses, net of divested operations, increased $29.1 million, or 14%, from $205.6 million in 2009 to $234.7 million in 2010.&#160;&#160;The cost of petroleum products increased $31.3 million, or 21%, due to higher wholesale market prices for petroleum products.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other operating expenses, net of divested operations, decreased $2.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2010 due primarily to a decrease in operating expenses related to reduced volumes, savings related to an overall cost reduction plan, and a reduction in uncollectible accounts.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For the year ended December 31, 2009, operating expenses, net of divested operations, decreased $121.0 million, or 37%, from $326.6 million in 2008 to $205.6 million in 2009.&#160;&#160;The cost of petroleum products decreased $117.1 million, or 44%, due to lower wholesale market prices and a decrease in sales volume.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other operating expenses decreased $4.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2009 due primarily to lower costs associated with lower oil prices, effective cost reduction initiatives, and the mid-December 2009 divestiture.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Businesses and Investments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenues and Operating Expenses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Revenue and operating expenses of other businesses and investments include the results of operations of Lyonsdale, CH-Greentree, CH-Auburn and CH Shirley Wind and are included in the Consolidated Financial Statements of CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;Results for the year ended December 31, 2010 compared to the same period in 2009 reflect an increase in operating revenues of $2.2 million and an increase in operating expenses of $3.8 million.&#160;&#160;The increase in revenues and a portion of the increase in operating expenses relate to CH-Greentree, which began commercial operation in the second half of 2009, and CH-Auburn, which became operational in February 2010.&#160;&#160;&#160;Additionally impacting the increases in operating expenses is an impairment on Lyonsdale assets of $2.1 million recorded in December 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Results for the year ended December 31, 2009 compared to the same period in 2008 reflect a decrease in operating revenues of $1.2 million and essentially no change in operating expenses with a net decrease in CH Energy Group&#8217;s net income of $0.5 million.&#160;&#160;This is primarily attributable to the outage for equipment repairs at Lyonsdale in the second quarter of 2009.&#160;&#160;CH-Greentree<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>became operational in the third quarter of 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Income and Interest Charges</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other income and deductions and interest charges for the balance of CH Energy Group, primarily the holding company and CHEC&#8217;s investments in partnerships and other investments (other than Griffith) for the year ended December 31, 2010 decreased by $10.6 million and increased $1.2 million as compared to the same period in 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;The decrease in other income and deductions is primarily the result of an impairment charge for 100% of CHEC&#8217;s subordinated debt, accrued interest and equity investment in Cornhusker Holdings totaling $11.4 million.&#160;&#160;This decrease in earnings was partially reduced by an increase in year-over-year results related to the write-off of $1.3 million recorded in the first quarter of 2009 related to a development project of CHEC.&#160;&#160;The increase in interest charges is due to the private placement of debt by the holding company in the second quarter of 2009 to fund unregulated portions of CH Energy Group.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other income and deductions and interest charges for the balance of CH Energy Group, primarily the holding company and CHEC&#8217;s investments in partnerships and other investments (other than Griffith), decreased $3.4 million and increased $1.9 million for the year ended December 31, 2009, when compared to the same period in 2008.&#160;&#160;This decrease includes the write-off of $1.3 million for the full amount related to the development project discussed above and the lower earnings at the partnerships.&#160;&#160;The increase in interest expense is related to the private placement of debt at the holding company in the second quarter of 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income taxes on income from continuing operations for CH Energy Group&#160;decreased $1.4&#160;million for the year ended December 31, 2010, compared to the same period in 2009, primarily due to the impact of a one-time reclassification of funded deferred taxes to a regulatory liability, resulting in a reduction to the tax provision of $2.3 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Income taxes on income from continuing operations for CH Energy Group increased $1.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2009, when compared to the same period in 2008 due to an increase in pre-tax book income and higher taxes incurred at the holding company resulting primarily from the gain on the sale of Griffith&#8217;s operations in certain geographic locations.&#160;&#160;Income taxes on income from discontinued operations increased $4.5 million due to an increase in pre-tax book income related to the discontinued operations as well as higher taxes incurred by Griffith as a result of the gain on the Griffith sale.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For all three years, both CH Energy Group&#8217;s and Central Hudson&#8217;s working capital needs were provided by cash from operations and in 2009 and 2008 were supplemented with short term financing as needed.&#160;&#160;Capital expenditures and investments in all three years were funded primarily with excess cash from operations and long term financing.&#160;&#160;In 2010, strong cash flows at Central Hudson as a result of a decrease in working capital needs at the end of 2009 and cash received from Federal and NYS income tax refunds enabled Central Hudson to accelerate funding of its pension plan.&#160;&#160;At CH Energy Group, cash on hand from the Griffith divestiture in December 2009 was used to fund capital expenditures for Shirley Wind in 2010.&#160;&#160;Additional discussions regarding cash flow from operating, investing and financing activities for each period are provided below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For all three periods and for both CH Energy Group and Central Hudson, cash provided by sales was used primarily to fund operating expenses and working capital needs.&#160;&#160;&#160;Incremental storm costs of $19.7 million incurred during the first quarter of 2010 as a result of the most significant storm event in Central Hudson&#8217;s history were funded primarily with financing activities and have been deferred for future recovery from customers.&#160;&#160;Lower working capital needs at the end of 2009 resulting from lower wholesale energy prices, as well as Federal and NYS income tax refunds received in 2010 as a result of a change in tax accounting method for repair and maintenance costs of Central Hudson&#8217;s utility assets, were used primarily to fund Central Hudson&#8217;s pension plan.&#160;&#160;Contributions to Central Hudson&#8217;s pension and OPEB plans totaled $69.6 million in 2010 as compared to $26.6 million in 2009 and $17.2 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;In 2009, Central Hudson&#8217;s cash from operations was also impacted by payments made to the PSC for a NYS temporary state assessment in advance of cash collections from customers.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s MGP site remediation costs in excess of amounts recovered through rates also impacted cash from operations for all three years, totaling $12.2 million in 2010, $2.3 million in 2009 and $2.8 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;Increased costs in 2010 for the completion of remediation at the Newburgh site were funded partially through an increase in delivery rates effective July 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;Costs above the rate allowance have been deferred for future recovery from customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Net cash used in investing activities was primarily related to investments in Central Hudson&#8217;s electric and natural gas transmission and distribution systems.&#160;&#160;Additionally, in June 2009, Central Hudson closed on the purchase of certain real-estate in Kingston, NY, resulting in an increase of approximately $13.0 million to plant additions in the prior year.&#160;&#160;Additional significant investing activities at CH Energy Group included capital expenditures related to the Shirley Wind construction of $29.6 million in 2010 funded primarily with cash from Griffith&#8217;s partial divestiture in December 2009 and $13.3 million in 2009 funded with long term debt issued by the holding company.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s investing activities include Griffith&#8217;s fuel distribution acquisitions in 2008 and 2010, as well as modest investments in property and plant in all three years.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Financing activities for both CH Energy Group and Central Hudson were used primarily to fund capital expenditures and to refinance maturing and redeemed debt.&#160;&#160;In 2010, proceeds from the sale of medium term notes at fixed interest rates were used to retire Central Hudson&#8217;s NYSERDA Series C and D variable rate debt prior to maturity.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson received $25 million in capital contributions from CH Energy Group in 2009, which was used to supplement the funding of investing activities.&#160;&#160;In 2009, CH Energy Group&#8217;s holding company sold $50 million of 5-year notes to provide financing for Shirley Wind.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group paid annual dividends to holders of common stock at an annual rate of $2.16 per share in all three years.&#160;&#160;After retaining earnings for several years to increase its equity ratio, Central Hudson began paying dividends to parent CH Energy Group in 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Capitalization &#8211; Issuance of Treasury Stock</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In May 2010, performance shares earned as of December 31, 2009 for the award cycle with a grant date of January 25, 2007 were issued to participants.&#160;&#160;Those recipients electing not to defer this compensation under the CH Energy Group Directors and Executives Deferred Compensation Plan received shares issued from CH Energy Group's treasury stock.&#160;&#160;A total of 9,983 shares were issued from CH Energy Group's treasury stock in May 2010.&#160;&#160;Additionally, due to the retirement of one of Central Hudson's executive officers on January 1, 2010, a pro-rated number of shares under the January 24, 2008 and January 26, 2009 grants were paid to this individual on July 1, 2010.&#160;&#160;An additional 2,134 shares were issued from CH Energy Group's treasury stock on this date in satisfaction of these awards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For further information regarding the above equity compensation, see Note 11 - &#8220;Equity Based Compensation&#8221; of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.&#160;&#160;The Company intends to continue to utilize shares issued from CH Energy Group&#8217;s treasury stock for the payout of future performance awards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Capital Structure</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s consolidated capital structure reflects the external debt and preferred stock of Central Hudson and privately placed external debt at CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;CHEC&#8217;s long-term debt is comprised entirely of intercompany loans from CH Energy Group that are eliminated upon consolidation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson has been gradually increasing its equity ratio in recent years to bolster its credit quality with the expectation that it would earn a return on the incremental equity through future delivery rates.&#160;&#160;Effective July 1, 2010, Central Hudson operated under the 2010 Rate Order and delivery rates are based on a capital structure that reflects 48% common equity.&#160;&#160;This ratio is calculated according to a PSC methodology, which excludes short-term debt.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson paid common stock dividends of $31 million to CH Energy Group in 2010.&#160;&#160;Dividends are expected to correspond to maintenance of a target equity ratio of approximately 48%, excluding short-term debt, in 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s current senior unsecured debt rating/outlook is &#8216;A&#8217;/stable by both Standard &amp; Poor&#8217;s Rating Services (&#8220;Standard &amp; Poor&#8217;s&#8221;) and Fitch Ratings and &#8216;A3&#8217;/stable by Moody&#8217;s Investors Service (&#8220;Moody&#8217;s&#8221;).<font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">(1)</font></font></font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson has an obligation to meet its contractual benefit payment obligations.&#160;&#160;Decisions about how to fund the Retirement Plan to meet these obligations are made at least annually and are primarily affected by the discount rate used to determine benefit obligations, current asset values, the projection of Retirement Plan assets and corporate resources.&#160;&#160;Based on the funding requirements of the Pension Protection Act, Central Hudson plans to make contributions that maintain the target funded percentage at 80% or higher.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s contribution in 2010 to fund the Retirement Plan was $64.2 million and its 2011 contribution is expected to total approximately $32 million, resulting in a funded status that meets Central Hudson&#8217;s objective.&#160;&#160;The actual contributions could vary significantly based upon actual and projected investment returns, interest rate assumptions and corporate resources.&#160;&#160;Actual funded status could vary significantly based on asset returns and changes in the discount rate used to estimate the present value of future obligations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s contributions in 2010 to fund OPEBs were $4.8 million.&#160;&#160;Obligations for future funding depend on a number of factors, including the discount rate, expected return, and medical claims assumptions used.&#160;&#160;If these factors remain stable, OPEB contributions over the next year are expected to be $1.2 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2010, the value of the Retirement Plan and OPEB assets increased by $82.7 million and $10.2 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;However, the decrease in discount rates from 2009 increased the present value of the plans&#8217; liabilities.&#160;&#160;The net effect on the funded status of the plans from the financial markets and the discount rates was a decrease in the unfunded status of the plans.&#160;&#160;Additional contributions will likely become necessary under the terms of the Pension Protection Act of 2006.&#160;&#160;Management expects that such contributions will be recovered through the rate making process over time.&#160;&#160;During the first quarter of 2010, Management began a transition to a long-duration investment strategy that is intended to reduce the year-to-year volatility of the funded status of the plan and of the level of contributions by more closely aligning the characteristics of plan assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Management cannot currently predict what impact future financial market volatility may have on the funded status of the plan or future funding decisions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Under the policy of the PSC regarding pension and OPEB costs, Central Hudson recovers these costs through customer rates with differences between actual cost and rate allowances deferred for future recovery from or return to customers.&#160;&#160;Based on the current policy, Central Hudson expects to fully recover its net periodic pension and OPEB costs over time.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Anticipated Sources and Uses of Cash</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s cash flow is primarily generated by the operations of its direct subsidiaries, Central Hudson and CHEC.&#160;&#160;Generally, the subsidiaries do not accumulate cash but rather provide cash to CH Energy Group in the form of dividends and, in the case of CHEC, repayments on its intercompany loans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s planned capital expenditures for construction and removal during 2011 total approximately $93 million.&#160;&#160;For 2012, planned capital expenditures are expected to fall within a range of $104 million to $114 million.&#160;&#160;Capital expenditures are expected to be funded with cash from operations and a combination of short-term and long-term borrowings.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson may alter its plan for capital expenditures as its business needs require.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson intends to fund growth in its long-lived assets in a manner that maintains an equity ratio of approximately 48% excluding short-term debt balances.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson plans to utilize short-term debt to fund seasonal and temporary variations in working capital requirements.&#160;&#160;If wholesale energy prices increase, Central Hudson would expect a corresponding increase from its current level of working capital. </font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Excluding acquisitions, capital expenditures at Griffith are expected to be approximately $2.4 million during 2011 and to range from $2.0 million to $2.5 million in 2012.&#160;&#160;In accordance with its business strategy, Griffith intends to fund any acquisitions from internally generated cash flow.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Griffith is financed by intercompany loans and equity investments from CH Energy Group in a manner that maintains an equity ratio of approximately 55% before seasonal working capital needs.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group plans to utilize short-term debt to fund seasonal and short-term variations in Griffith&#8217;s working capital needs.&#160;&#160;If wholesale energy prices increase, Griffith would expect a corresponding increase from its current level of working capital.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group believes cash generated from operations and funds obtained from its financing program will be sufficient in 2011 and the foreseeable future to meet working capital needs, pay dividends on its Common Stock, and fund investments and acquisitions to fulfill its public service obligations and growth objectives.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s primary source of funds is the cash it generates from the operations of Central Hudson and CHEC, which can be affected by volatility in energy markets that affects their working capital needs and profitability.&#160;&#160;Recent strategic decisions, including the divestiture of Griffith&#8217;s divisions in the Northeast in December 2009 and plans to evaluate the market and potentially divest non-core CHEC investments in unregulated energy production assets are expected to improve the stability of CH Energy Group&#8217;s cash flow and financing requirements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s secondary sources of funds are its cash reserves and its credit facility.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s ability to use its credit facility is contingent upon maintaining certain financial covenants.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group does not anticipate that those covenants will restrict its access to funds in 2011 or the foreseeable future.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective July 31, 2007, CH Energy Group&#8217;s Board of Directors extended and amended the Common Stock Repurchase Program of the Company (the &#8220;Repurchase Program&#8221;), which was originally authorized in 2002.&#160;&#160;As amended, the Repurchase Program authorizes the repurchase of up to 2,000,000 shares (excluding shares repurchased before July 31, 2007) or approximately 13% of the CH Energy Group&#8217;s outstanding Common Stock, from time to time, through July 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010 CH Energy Group had purchased 29,562 shares under the Repurchase Program.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to year-end and through February 1, 2011, CH Energy Group purchased 106,400 additional shares under the Repurchase Program.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group intends to purchase additional shares under the Program during 2011.&#160;&#160;No shares were purchased under the Repurchase Program in 2008 or 2009.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group intends to set repurchase targets, if any, from time to time based on then prevailing circumstances.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Financing Program</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group believes that it is well positioned with a strong balance sheet and strong liquidity.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group entered 2011 with no short-term debt liabilities and significant available capacity under CH Energy Group&#8217;s and Central Hudson&#8217;s committed credit facilities.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s strong investment-grade credit ratings help facilitate access to long-term debt; however, despite improving conditions in financial markets, Management can make no assurance regarding the availability of financing or its terms and costs.&#160;&#160;With the exception of treasury shares to be issued for several restricted share grants and performance share awards earned, no equity issuance is currently planned for 2011.&#160;&#160;As discussed earlier, CH Energy Group is actively seeking to divest CHEC assets, and it plans to use net proceeds primarily for the repurchase of common stock and the repayment of debt associated with those assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group maintains a $150 million revolving credit agreement with several commercial banks to provide committed liquidity beyond its cash balance.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, CH Energy Group had no outstanding borrowings under its credit agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group has used approximately $25 million of the proceeds from the December 2009 sale of notes, to fund a portion of its investment in the Shirley Wind project.&#160;&#160;Construction on this project is nearly complete and it is currently undergoing final testing prior to final acceptance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson has a $125 million committed credit agreement with several commercial banks, which expires January 2, 2012.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson expects to negotiate a new multi-year revolving credit facility during 2011.&#160;&#160;In addition to this credit agreement, Central Hudson maintains several uncommitted lines of credit with various banks.&#160;&#160;These arrangements give Central Hudson competitive options to minimize the cost of its short-term borrowings.&#160;&#160;At December 31, 2010, Central Hudson had no outstanding balance under its uncommitted lines of credit and no outstanding balance under its committed credit agreement.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The lenders under both the CH Energy Group ($150 million) and Central Hudson ($125 million) credit agreements include JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A., Bank of America N.A., HSBC Bank USA N.A. and KeyBank N.A..&#160;&#160;The availability of these facilities is contingent upon the ability of the lenders to fulfill their commitments.&#160;&#160;If one or more banks are deemed at risk of being unable to meet their commitments, CH Energy Group and Central Hudson may seek alternative sources of committed credit to supplement the current agreements.&#160;&#160;However, alternate sources may not be readily available. CH Energy Group and Central Hudson plan for such a situation by reserving portions of the total commitment for unforeseen events.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson meets its need for long-term debt financing through a medium-term notes program and privately placed debt.&#160;&#160;As a regulated electric and natural gas utility company, Central Hudson is required to obtain authorization from the PSC to issue securities with maturities greater than 12 months.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On September 22, 2009, the PSC authorized Central Hudson to increase its multi-year committed credit to $175 million and to issue up to $250 million of long-term debt through December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;The Order authorized Central Hudson to issue and sell $250 million of long-term debt to finance its construction expenditures, refund maturing long-term debt, and refinance its 1999 NYSERDA Bonds, Series B, C and D.&#160;&#160;As discussed below, Series C and D have been refinanced under this provision.&#160;&#160;A new shelf registration statement was filed by Central Hudson with the SEC covering the offer and sale of up to $250 million of long-term debt pursuant to the authority granted by the PSC.&#160;&#160;An amendment to the registration statement was filed on December 23, 2009 and the registration became effective on January 6, 2010.&#160;&#160;No immediate action is planned to increase Central Hudson&#8217;s committed credit; however, options to do so will be evaluated during 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On September 21, 2010, Central Hudson entered into a Note Purchase Agreement to issue and sell, in a private placement exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, $40 million of senior unsecured notes in two series.&#160;&#160;Series A notes bear interest at the rate of 4.30% per annum on a principal amount of $16 million and mature on September 21, 2020.&#160;&#160;Series B notes bear interest at the rate of 5.64% per annum on a principal amount of $24 million and matures on September 21, 2040.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson used a portion of the proceeds from the sale of the notes for refunding maturing long-term debt and retained the remainder for general corporate purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson has three outstanding series, totaling $84 million in principal amount, which were issued in conjunction with the sale of tax-exempt pollution control revenue bonds by NYSERDA.&#160;&#160;These NYSERDA bonds are insured by Ambac Assurance Corporation (&#8220;Ambac&#8221;), and the ratings on these bonds reflect the higher of the credit rating of Ambac or Central Hudson.&#160;&#160;The current underlying rating and outlook on these bonds and Central Hudson&#8217;s other senior unsecured debt is &#8216;A&#8217;/stable by Standard &amp; Poor&#8217;s and Fitch Ratings and &#8216;A3&#8217;/stable by Moody&#8217;s.<font style="FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">(2)</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s 1998 NYSERDA Series A Bonds, totaling $16.7 million, were re-marketed on December 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the applicable indenture, Central Hudson converted the bonds to a fixed rate of 6.5% per annum, which will continue until their maturity in December 2028.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s 1999 NYSERDA Series A Bonds, totaling $33.4 million, have an interest rate that is fixed to maturity in 2027 at 5.45% per annum.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s Series B 1999 NYSERDA Bonds total $33.7 million and are tax-exempt multi-modal bonds that are currently in a variable rate mode.&#160;&#160;In its Orders, the PSC has authorized deferral accounting treatment for variations in the interest costs from these bonds.&#160;&#160;As such, variations between the actual interest rates on these bonds and the interest rate included in the current delivery rate structure for these bonds are deferred for future recovery from or refund to customers. As a result, variations in interest rates do not have any impact on earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson had an additional $82.15 million in notes outstanding in 2010 consisting of Series C and Series D 1999 NYSERDA Bonds.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson felt that the terms of this variable rate debt could expose the delivery rate structure to volatile and high interest rate costs.&#160;&#160;After evaluating the alternatives in light of the prevailing market conditions, Central Hudson retired both Series on December 27, 2010 through the issuance of $82.15 million in Series G notes under Central Hudson&#8217;s Medium Term Note program.&#160;&#160;No Bonds of either Series remain outstanding.&#160;&#160;Costs incurred in the issuance of the unsecured Series G Medium Term Notes have been allocated proportionately across the issuances and will be amortized over their respective terms.&#160;&#160;Unamortized costs written off in the retirement of the Series C and D NYSERDA bonds have been deferred as a regulatory asset and will be amortized over the original term of the bonds.&#160;&#160;The amortization of debt costs for both outstanding and redeemed debt are incorporated in the revenue requirement for delivery rates as authorized by the PSC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To mitigate the potential cash flow impact of unexpected increases in short-term interest rates, Central Hudson purchases interest rate caps based on an index of short-term tax-exempt debt.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s one year rate caps for its NYSERDA Bonds, set at 3.0%, expired on March 31, 2010 and were replaced with three new rate caps.&#160;&#160;Effective April 1, 2010, the new rate caps are set at 5.0%.&#160;&#160;Two of the rate caps were one-year in length with notional amounts aligned to Series C and Series D NYSERDA Bonds and are no longer outstanding.&#160;&#160;These two rate caps will expire on April 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;The third rate cap is two years in length with a notional amount aligned with the Series B NYSERDA Bonds and will expire on April 1, 2012.&#160;&#160;The caps are based on the monthly weighted average of an index of tax-exempt variable rate debt, multiplied by 175%.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson would receive a payout if the adjusted index exceeds 5.0% for a particular month.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Energy Efficiency Portfolio Standard and State Energy Planning</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Case 07-M-0548 - Proceeding on Motion of the PSC Regarding an Energy Efficiency Portfolio Standard and Governor Paterson&#8217;s Executive Order issued April 9, 2008)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Background:</font>&#160;&#160;New York State has established a goal of substantially reducing electricity usage and created a State Energy Planning Board which is authorized to create and implement a State Energy Plan (&#8220;SEP&#8221;).&#160;&#160;In support of this goal, the PSC is investigating various approaches to reduce customers&#8217; demand for energy and to provide utility incentives for meeting specified energy savings targets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On January 7, 2009 Governor Patterson outlined various strategies and policy goals in his State of the State address, including one of the most aggressive clean energy goals in the country, with a goal for New York to meet 45% of its electricity needs by 2015 (&#8220;45 x 15&#8221;) through improved energy efficiency and clean renewable energy production by expanding the Renewable Portfolio Standard from 25% by 2013 to 30% by 2015 and decreasing electric usage by 15% by 2015.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notable Activity:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2009 and 2010 Central Hudson received approval through the Energy Efficiency Portfolio Standard (&#8220;EEPS&#8221;) proceedings to implement various programs to electric and natural gas residential and commercial customers.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In December 2010, the PSC issued an Order combining energy savings targets to create a single 2008-2011 target and continuing the system of utility shareholder financial incentives established in the EEPS proceeding.&#160;&#160;Calendar year targets will be in effect for 2012 and beyond.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Potential Impacts:</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>This PSC proceeding could result in opportunities for increased earnings from incentives associated with achieving energy efficiency targets, or could result in negative rate adjustments if the 70% performance criterion is not met.&#160;&#160;No prediction can be made regarding the final outcome of this matter; however, any earnings variations are not likely to be material.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font><br>
&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Petition of Central Hudson Gas &amp; Electric Corporation for Commission Approval of a Plan for Deferred Accounting for Future Recovery with Carrying Charges of Three Items and Funding These and Certain Other Deferrals through Balance Sheet Offsets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Case 10-M-0473)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Background:</font>&#160;&#160;On September 23, 2010, Central Hudson filed a petition with the PSC to defer for future recovery with carrying charges $19.4 million incremental electric storm restoration expense, $2.6 million incremental electric bad debt write-off expense, $1.9 million incremental electric property tax expense and $0.7 million incremental gas property tax expense above the respective rate allowances during the twelve months ended June 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;The petition also requests approval of offsets of the foregoing against significant tax refunds resulting from a change in the way Central Hudson treats certain capital expenditures for tax purposes.&#160;&#160;Additional offsets against other deferred items, notably including MGP site investigation and remediation costs were also included in the petition given the size of the tax refunds.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Advanced Metering Infrastructure</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Case 09-M-0074 - Proceeding on Matter of Advanced Metering Infrastructure)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Case 10-E-0285 - Proceeding on Motion of the Commission to Consider Regulatory Policies Regarding Smart Grid Systems and the Modernization of the Electric Grid)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Background:</font>&#160;&#160;On February 13, 2009, the PSC issued an Order establishing minimum functional requirements for Advanced Metering Infrastructure (&#8220;AMI&#8221;) in New York State and creating a process for the development of a generic approach to the benefit/cost analysis of AMI.&#160;&#160;The filing requirements set forth by the PSC in the Order were designed to put utilities on track to potentially receive federal financial assistance that may become available under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009&#8217;s (&#8220;ARRA&#8221;) Department of Energy (&#8220;DOE&#8221;) administered program for Electricity Delivery and Energy Reliability (&#8220;EDER&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The DOE may provide grants to successful applicants under the EDER program in an amount equal to not more than 50% of the costs of qualifying investments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notable Activity:&#160;&#160;</font>In July 2010, the PSC closed Case 09-M-0074 and initiated a new proceeding, Case 10-E-0285 to determine to what extent further development of regulatory policies should be made to encourage electric utilities to develop smart grid systems that can facilitate the integration of new technologies while optimizing their efficient use of facilities and resources, and producing equitable rates for electric customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">The ARRA Project Funding</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Case 09-E-0310 - In the Matter of American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 - Utility Filings for New York Economic Stimulus)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Background:</font>&#160;&#160;ARRA includes a DOE administered program for EDER.&#160;&#160;The sum of $4.5 billion is appropriated by ARRA for the EDER program to be dispersed by DOE through a competitive grant process.&#160;&#160;Additional funds may also be available through programs such as Transportation Electrification.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Management Audit</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(Case 09-M-07674 &#8211; Comprehensive Management Audit of Central Hudson Gas &amp; Electric Business)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Background:</font>&#160;&#160;In February 2010, the PSC selected NorthStar Consulting Group (&#8220;NorthStar&#8221;) as the independent third-party consultant to conduct a comprehensive management audit of Central Hudson&#8217;s construction planning processes and operational efficiencies of its electric and gas businesses.&#160;&#160;The PSC is allowed to audit New York utilities every five years.&#160;&#160;Audit work officially commenced on March 24, 2010.&#160;&#160;NorthStar issued its Draft Audit Report December 6, 2010. Central Hudson will have an opportunity to make factual corrections to the draft report.&#160;&#160;A final report to the PSC of NorthStar&#8217;s findings and recommendations is expected in the first quarter of 2011.&#160;&#160;No prediction can be made regarding the outcome of the matter at this time however, any recommendations will require a corresponding implementation plan for improvement as well as progress updates in future quarterly filings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">OTHER MATTERS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Changes In Accounting Standards</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See Note&#160;3 - &#8220;New Accounting Guidance&#8221; for a discussion of the status of new accounting guidance issued.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group and Central Hudson do not have any off-balance sheet arrangements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Retirement Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See Note 10 &#8211; &#8220;Post-Employment Benefits&#8221; and Critical Accounting Policies for a discussion of the Retirement Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Climate</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">While it is possible that some form of global climate change program will be adopted at the federal level in 2011, it is too early to determine what impact such program will have on CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;It should be noted, however, that the Company's calculated CO<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: sub">2</font> emission levels are relatively small, primarily because the Company does not generate electricity in significant quantities and the electricity it does generate is from zero emission hydroelectric plants.&#160;&#160;Therefore, federally mandated greenhouse gas reductions or limits on CO<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: sub">2</font> emissions are not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial position or results of operations.&#160;&#160;However, the Company can make no prediction as to the outcome of this matter.&#160;&#160;If the cost of CO<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: sub">2</font> emissions causes purchased electricity and natural gas costs to rise, such increases are expected to be collected through automatic adjustment clauses.&#160;&#160;If sales are depressed by higher costs through price elasticity, the RDMs are expected to prevent an earnings impact on the Company.</font></div>
