<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Financial Statements were prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), which for regulated public utilities, includes specific guidance for Regulated Operations.&#160;&#160;For additional information regarding regulatory accounting, see Note 2 &#8211; &#8220;Regulatory Matters.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Use of Estimates</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Preparation of the Consolidated Financial Statements in accordance with GAAP includes the use of estimates and assumptions by management that affect financial results.&#160;&#160;Actual results may differ from those estimated; however the methods used by CH Energy Group to prepare estimates have historically produced reliable results.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Expense items most affected by the use of estimates are depreciation and amortization (including amortization of intangible assets), reserves for uncollectible accounts receivable, other operating reserves, tax reserves, unbilled revenues, and pension and other post-retirement benefits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Depreciation and amortization is based on estimates of the useful lives and estimated net salvage value of properties.&#160;&#160;For Central Hudson, these estimates are subject to change as the result of a future rate proceeding.&#160;&#160;Historical changes have not been material to the Company&#8217;s financial results.&#160;&#160;For Griffith and CHEC&#8217;s other subsidiaries, any changes in estimates used for depreciation are not expected to have a material impact on CH Energy Group&#8217;s financial results.&#160;&#160;The amortization of CH Energy Group&#8217;s other intangible assets is discussed in detail below under the caption &#8220;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2010, Central Hudson elected to change its tax return methodology for claiming deductions for incidental repair and maintenance expenditures on its utility assets.&#160;&#160;The change accelerates the recognition of the tax deduction from later periods.&#160;&#160;Although the Company believes that its methodology for claiming the deduction is consistent with the Internal Revenue Code and case law, it is unclear whether the Internal Revenue Service will accept the entirety of the deduction claimed.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the Company has recorded a reserve based upon the expected outcome on audit.&#160;&#160;See Note 4 &#8211; &#8220;Income Taxes&#8221; for further discussion of the tax reserve established.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Estimates for uncollectible accounts are based on customer accounts receivable aging data as well as consideration of various quantitative and qualitative factors, including economic factors such as future outlooks for the economy, unemployment rates, energy prices and special collection issues.&#160;&#160;The estimates for other operating reserves are based on assessments of future obligations related to injuries and damages and workers compensation claims.&#160;&#160;Unbilled revenues are determined based on the estimated sales for bi-monthly accounts that have not been billed by Central Hudson in the current month.&#160;&#160;The estimation methods used in determining these sales are the same methods used for billing customers when actual meter readings cannot be obtained.&#160;&#160;Historical changes to these items have not been material to the Company&#8217;s financial results.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See Note 1 - &#8220;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; under the caption &#8220;Use of Estimates&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements of this 10-K Annual Report for additional discussion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The balances reflected on CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheet at December 31, 2010 and December 31, 2009 for &#8220;Goodwill&#8221; and &#8220;Other intangible assets - net&#8221; relate to Griffith.&#160;&#160;Goodwill represents the excess of cost over the fair value of the net tangible and identifiable intangible assets of businesses acquired as of the date of acquisition.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In accordance with current accounting guidance related to goodwill and other intangible assets, both goodwill and intangible assets not subject to amortization are tested at least annually for impairment and whenever events or circumstances make it more likely than not that an impairment may have occurred, such as a significant adverse change in the business climate or a decision to sell or dispose of a reporting unit.&#160;&#160;In assessing whether an impairment exists, the fair value of the reporting unit is compared to the carrying amount of assets.&#160;&#160;Fair value of goodwill is estimated using a weighted average of the discounted cash flow and market approach methodologies. In applying this methodology to the discounted cash flow, reliance is placed on a number of factors, including actual operating results, future business plans, economic projections and market data.&#160;&#160;The carrying amount for goodwill was $35.9 million as of December 31, 2010 and $35.7 million as of December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;Historical impairment tests have not resulted in the recognition of any impairment. However, if the operating cash flows of Griffith decline significantly relative to CH Energy Group&#8217;s investment in Griffith in the future, the result could be recognition of a future goodwill impairment charge to operations and the amount could be material to CH Energy Group's Consolidated Financial Statements.&#160;&#160;However, given the accelerated recovery of $10 million of goodwill as a result of the 2009 divestiture, and the significant excess of fair value over the book value of the Company, Management believes the likelihood of any such write-off is remote.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The most significant assumptions used in the discounted cash flow valuation regarding Griffith&#8217;s fair value in connection with goodwill valuations are: (1) detailed five-year cash flow projections, (2) the risk adjusted discount rate, and (3) Griffith&#8217;s expected long-term growth rate, which approximates the growth rate imputed from the discrete period cash flow projections on key aspects of the business.&#160;&#160;The primary drivers of Griffith's cash flow projections include sales volumes, margin rates and expense inflation, particularly for labor.&#160;&#160;The risk adjusted discount rate represents Griffith&#8217;s weighted average cost of capital and is established based on (1) the 30 year risk-free rate, which is impacted by events external to Griffith, such as investor expectations regarding economic activity, (2) Griffith&#8217;s indicated market rate of return on equity, and (3) the current after-tax rate of return on debt.&#160;&#160;In valuing its goodwill for 2010, Griffith used an average risk-adjusted discount rate of 10.4%.&#160;&#160;Had the risk-adjusted discount rate been 25 basis points higher, the aggregate estimated fair value of the reporting units would have decreased by $1.2 million, or 1.4%.&#160;&#160;In addition, Griffith used an average expected terminal growth rate of 0.5%.&#160;&#160;If the expected terminal growth rate was 25 basis points lower, the aggregate estimated fair value of the reporting units would have decreased by $0.8 million, or 0.9%.&#160;&#160;Had each year in Griffith&#8217;s five-year cash flow projections been lower by 1.0%, the aggregate estimated fair value of the reporting units would have decreased by $0.2 million, or 0.3%.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, the fair value of goodwill as calculated was approximately $34.2 million above its carrying value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other intangible assets - net relate to Griffith and are comprised of customer relationships, trademarks and covenants not to compete.&#160;&#160;If events indicate that an impairment exists, these assets are tested for impairment by comparing the carrying amount to the sum of undiscounted cash flows expected to be generated by the asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In accordance with current accounting guidance, intangible assets that have finite useful lives continue to be amortized over their useful lives.&#160;&#160;The estimated useful life for customer relationships is 15 years, which is believed to be appropriate in view of average historical customer attrition.&#160;&#160;The useful lives of trademarks were estimated to range from 10 to 15 years based upon Management&#8217;s assessment of several variables such as brand recognition, Management&#8217;s expected use of the trademark, and other factors that may have affected the duration of the trademark&#8217;s life.&#160;&#160;The useful life of a covenant not to compete is based on the expiration date of the covenant, generally between three and ten years.&#160;&#160;Amortization expense was $2.3 million, $4.0 million and $4.1 million for each of the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, respectively.&#160;&#160;The estimated annual amortization expense for each of the next five years, assuming no new acquisitions, is approximately $2.2 million.&#160;&#160;The weighted average amortization period for all amortizable intangible assets is 15 years.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>The weighted average amortization periods for customer relationships and covenants not to compete are 15 years and 5 years, respectively.&#160;&#160;The estimated useful life of Griffith&#8217;s customer relationships is tested annually based on actual experience.&#160;&#160;The amortizable life of these assets has not changed since Griffith was acquired.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See Note 6 - &#8220;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets&#8221; of this 10-K Annual Report for additional discussion.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Post-Employment Benefits</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In accordance with the terms of the 2006, 2009 and 2010 Rate Orders, Central Hudson is authorized to defer any differences between rate allowances and actual costs for both its Retirement and OPEB plans.&#160;&#160;As a result, Central Hudson expects to fully recover its net periodic pension and OPEB costs over time.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s reported costs of providing non-contributory defined pension benefits as well as certain health care and life insurance benefits for retired employees are dependent upon numerous factors resulting from actual plan experience and assumptions of future plan performance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The significant assumptions and estimates used to account for the Retirement Plan and other post-retirement benefit expenses and liabilities are the discount rate, the expected long-term rate of return on the pension plan and other post-retirement plan assets, health care cost trend rate, the rate of compensation increase, mortality assumptions and the method of amortizing gains and losses.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For 2010, the Projected Benefit Obligation (&#8220;PBO&#8221;) for Central Hudson&#8217;s Retirement Plan ($500.2 million) and its obligation for OPEB costs ($136.5 million) were determined using 5.3% and 5.2% discount rates, respectively.&#160;&#160;These rates were determined using the Citigroup Pension Discount Curve reflecting projected cash flows.&#160;&#160;A 0.25% change in the discount rate would affect the projection of the pension PBO by approximately $15.0&#160;million and the OPEB obligation by approximately $4.2 million.&#160;&#160;Investment losses in the years 2000 through 2002, and a reduction in the discount rate during that period have resulted in a significant increase in pension and OPEB costs since 2001.&#160;&#160;Declines in the market value of the Trust Funds investment portfolio in 2008 resulted in significant future increases in pension costs.&#160;&#160;During the years ended December 31, 2010 and 2009, Central Hudson contributed $64.2 million and $22.6 million to its Retirement Plan.&#160;&#160;During 2010, the value of the Retirement Plan and OPEB assets increased by $82.7 million and $10.2 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;These increases reduced the underfunded status of these plans.&#160;&#160;However, the decrease in discount rates from 2009 increased the present value of the plans&#8217; liabilities.&#160;&#160;The net effect on the funded status of the plans from the improved financial markets, increased contributions and the lower discount rates was a decrease in the unfunded liability by $49.8 million and $0.9 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;A 0.25% change in the discount rate would impact the net periodic benefit cost by $1.5 million for the Retirement Plan and $0.4 million for OPEBs.&#160;&#160;Additional contributions will likely become necessary under the terms of the Pension Protection Act of 2006.&#160;&#160;Management expects that such contributions will continue to be incorporated in the rate making process over time.&#160;&#160;The rate of compensation increase was based on historical and current compensation practices of Central Hudson giving consideration to any anticipated changes in this practice.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson has investment policies for these plans which include asset allocation ranges designed to achieve a reasonable return over the long-term, recognizing the impact of market volatility.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson monitors actual performance against target asset allocations and adjusts actual allocations and targets as deemed appropriate in accordance with the Retirement Plan strategy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounting for Long-lived Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Based on the change in strategy in the fourth quarter of 2010 discussed in the Executive Summary and the marketing efforts related to CHEC&#8217;s Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind investments that began later in the quarter, Management believes it is more likely than not that the long-lived assets of these investments will be sold before the end of their previously estimated useful lives.&#160; As of December 31, 2010, Management performed a test to evaluate whether&#160;the carrying amount of these assets exceeds the expected undiscounted cash flow from these assets over their estimated remaining useful lives and whether the carrying amount exceeds the estimated fair value of these assets, which would require the recognition of an impairment.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For Lyonsdale, Management performed the test using bids received from several parties in early&#160;2011.&#160; Management believes these proposals represent a market participant&#8217;s fair value of the investment.&#160; The current proposals indicate it is unlikely that CHEC will receive book value under such sale.&#160; Accordingly, Management recorded a pre-tax impairment of $2.1 million ($1.3 million after-tax impact on earnings) as of December 31, 2010, based on the amount by which the carrying amount exceeded the fair value of&#160;these assets.&#160; Management cannot predict the final outcome of the sale process.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For Shirley Wind, Management estimated the future cash flows from internal data and from indicative bids received in January 2011 as part of the on-going marketing efforts.&#160; No impairment was indicated by either of these analyses.&#160; However, Management cannot predict the final outcome of the sale process.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The remaining renewable energy investments will be evaluated in 2011 to determine if an opportunity exists to divest these investments in a manner that maximizes shareholder value.&#160; Management cannot predict the outcome of this market analysis.&#160; However, Management has reviewed CH-Auburn and CH-Greentree as of December 31, 2010 based on an undiscounted cash flow analysis of operations and does not believe these assets are impaired.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounting for Derivatives</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries use derivatives to manage their commodity and financial market risks; they do not enter into derivative instruments for speculative purposes.&#160;&#160;As a result of deferrals under Central Hudson&#8217;s regulatory mechanisms and offsetting changes of commodity prices for both Central Hudson and Griffith, derivatives that CH Energy Group and Central Hudson enter into do not materially impact earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">All derivatives, other than those specifically excepted, are reported on the Consolidated Balance Sheet at fair value.&#160;&#160;For discussions relating to market risk and derivative instruments, see Item 7A - &#8220;Quantitative and Qualitative disclosure About Market Risk&#8221; and Note 14 - &#8220;Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#8221; of this 10-K Annual Report.</font></div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr>
<td align="left" valign="top" width="93%"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="item7a">ITEM 7A</a> - </font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosure About Market Risk</font></td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The practices employed by CH Energy Group and Central Hudson to mitigate risks discussed below continue to operate effectively.&#160;&#160;For related discussion on this activity, see Item 7 - &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221; under the sub-caption &#8220;Capital Resources and Liquidity,&#8221; Note 14 - &#8220;Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&#8221; and Note 9 - "Long-Term Debt" within this 10-K Annual Report.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The primary market risks for CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries and investments are commodity price risk and interest rate risk.&#160;&#160;Commodity price risk, related primarily to purchases of natural gas, electricity, and petroleum products for resale to retail customers, is mitigated in several different ways.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson, as authorized by the PSC, collects its actual purchased electricity and purchased natural gas costs from its customers through cost adjustment clauses in its rates.&#160;&#160;These adjustment clauses provide for the collection of costs, including risk management and working capital costs, to reflect the actual costs incurred in obtaining supply.&#160;&#160;Risk management costs are defined by the PSC as &#8220;costs associated with transactions that are intended to reduce price volatility or reduce overall costs to customers.&#160;&#160;These costs include transaction costs and gains and losses associated with risk management instruments.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Depending on market conditions, Central Hudson may enter into long-term fixed supply and long-term forward supply contracts for the purchase of these commodities.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson also uses natural gas storage facilities, which enable it to purchase and hold quantities of natural gas at pre-heating season prices for use during the heating season.&#160;&#160;Griffith may increase the prices charged for the commodities it sells in response to changes in costs; however, its ability to raise prices is generally limited by what the competitive market in which it participates will bear.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson and Griffith have in place an energy risk management program within their operations.&#160;&#160;This risk management program permits the use of derivative financial instruments for hedging purposes but does not permit their use for trading or speculative purposes.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson and Griffith have entered into either exchange-traded futures contracts or over-the-counter (&#8220;OTC&#8221;) contracts with third parties to hedge commodity price risk associated with the purchase of natural gas, electricity, and petroleum products and to hedge the effect on earnings due to significant variations in weather conditions from historical patterns.&#160;&#160;The types of derivative instruments typically used include natural gas futures and swaps to hedge natural gas purchases, contracts for differences to hedge electricity purchases, put and call options to hedge oil purchases, and degree-day based weather derivatives to hedge weather variations.&#160;&#160;In this latter case, Griffith uses such derivative instruments to dampen the impact of weather variations on delivery revenues.&#160;&#160;OTC derivative transactions are entered into only with counterparties that meet certain credit criteria.&#160;&#160;The creditworthiness of these counterparties is determined primarily by reference to published credit ratings.&#160;&#160;Commodity price risk related to both corn and ethanol is managed by Cornhusker Holdings at the entity level, not by CHEC or CH Energy Group directly.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The use of derivative instruments for hedging purposes is discussed in more detail in Note 14 -&#8220;Accounting for Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities,&#8221; which incorporates sensitivity analysis for each type of derivative instrument.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Interest rate risk affects Central Hudson but is managed through the issuance of fixed-rate debt with varying maturities and of variable rate debt for which interest is reset on a periodic basis to reflect current market conditions.&#160;&#160;In the case of Central Hudson&#8217;s variable rate debt, the difference between costs associated with actual variable interest rates and costs embedded in customer rates is deferred for eventual refund to or recovery from customers.&#160;&#160;The variability in interest rates is also managed with the use of a derivative financial instrument known as an interest rate cap agreement, for which the premium cost and any realized benefits also pass through the aforementioned regulatory recovery mechanism.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson replaced an expiring rate cap, effective April 1, 2010, with two one-year rate cap agreements covering certain issues of variable rate 1999 NYSERDA Bonds and a two-year rate cap covering another issue of such debt.&#160;&#160;The caps are based on the monthly weighted average of an index of tax-exempt variable rate debt, multiplied by 175% to align with the maximum rate formula of the three series of the 1999 NYSERDA Bonds.&#160;&#160;The interest rate caps are evaluated quarterly and Central Hudson, under the terms of all three caps, would receive a payout for a particular series if the variable rate for the bonds of that series reset at rates above 5.0%.&#160;&#160;All three rate cap agreements were made with KeyBank National Association.&#160;&#160;Please refer to Note 9 - &#8220;Capitalization - Long-Term Debt,&#8221; Note 15 - &#8220;Fair Value Measurements&#8221; and Item 7 - &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8221; under the sub-caption &#8220;Capital Resources and Liquidity&#8221; for additional disclosure related to long-term debt.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="REPORTACCOUNTINGFIRM">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To the Board of Directors and Shareholders of CH Energy Group, Inc.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements listed in the accompanying index present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of CH Energy Group, Inc. and its subsidiaries (collectively, the "Company") at December 31, 2010 and 2009, and the results of their operations and their cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2010 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.&#160;&#160;In addition, in our opinion, the financial statement schedules listed in the accompanying index<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#160;</font>present fairly, in all material respects, the information set forth therein when read in conjunction with the related consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;Also in our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2010, based on criteria established in <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Internal Control - Integrated Framework</font> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).&#160;&#160;The Company's management is responsible for these financial statements and financial statement schedules for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying CH Energy Group Report of Management on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.&#160;&#160;Our responsibility is to express opinions on these financial statements, on the financial statement schedules, and on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our integrated audits.&#160;&#160;We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States).&#160;&#160;Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement and whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.&#160;&#160;Our audits of the financial statements included examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.&#160;&#160;Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk.&#160;&#160;Our audits also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.&#160;&#160;We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&#160;&#160;A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (i)&#160;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (ii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (iii)&#160;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&#160;&#160;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="REPORTMGMT">CH ENERGY GROUP</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Report of Management on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The management of CH Energy Group, Inc. (&#8220;Management&#8221;) is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting for CH Energy Group, Inc. (the &#8220;Corporation&#8221;) as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.&#160;&#160;Internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.&#160;&#160;Internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the Corporation;</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America and that receipts and expenditures of the Corporation are being made only in accordance with authorization of Management and directors of the Corporation; and</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" id="list" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">
<tr valign="top">
<td align="right" style="WIDTH: 72pt">
<div><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" face="Symbol, serif">&#183;&#160;&#160;</font></div>
</td>
<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of assets that could have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Internal control over financial reporting includes the controls themselves, monitoring (including internal auditing practices) and actions taken to correct deficiencies as identified.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&#160;&#160;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management assessed the effectiveness of the Corporation&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Management based this assessment on criteria for effective internal control over financial reporting described in &#8220;<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Internal Control - Integrated Framework</font>&#8221; issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).&#160;&#160;Based on this assessment, Management determined that, as of December 31, 2010, the Corporation maintained effective internal control over financial reporting.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note1">NOTE 1</a> &#8211; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Organization</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group, Inc. (&#8220;CH Energy Group&#8221;) is the holding company parent corporation of Central Hudson Gas&#160;&amp; Electric Corporation (&#8220;Central Hudson&#8221;) and Central Hudson Enterprises Corporation (&#8220;CHEC&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Central Hudson and CHEC are each wholly owned by CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;Their businesses are comprised of a regulated electric utility and regulated natural gas utility, fuel distribution, and investments in renewable energy projects.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CHEC&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiaries include:&#160;&#160;Griffith Energy Service, Inc. (&#8220;Griffith&#8221;), CH-Auburn Energy, LLC (&#8220;CH-Auburn&#8221;), CH-Greentree, LLC (&#8220;CH-Greentree&#8221;), CH-Lyonsdale, LLC (&#8220;CH-Lyonsdale&#8221;), Lyonsdale Biomass, LLC (&#8220;Lyonsdale&#8221;) and CH Shirley Wind, LLC (&#8220;CH Shirley&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 1, 2010, CHEC purchased the minority owner&#8217;s 25% interest in Lyonsdale Biomass, LLC (&#8220;Lyonsdale&#8221;) and now is the 100% owner.&#160;&#160;The operating results of Lyonsdale are consolidated in the financial statements of CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;The non-controlling interest shown on CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Financial Statements for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008 includes the minority owner&#8217;s proportionate share of the income and equity of Lyonsdale prior to this purchase.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 15, 2009, CH Shirley purchased a 90% interest in Shirley Wind (Delaware), LLC (&#8220;Shirley Delaware&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The operating results of Shirley Delaware are consolidated in the financial statements of CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;The non-controlling interest shown on CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended December 31, 2010 and 2009 includes the minority owner&#8217;s proportionate share of the income and equity of Shirley Delaware.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CHEC&#8217;s investments in limited partnerships (&#8220;Partnerships&#8221;) and limited liability companies are accounted for under the equity method.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s proportionate share of the change in fair value of available for sale securities held by the Partnerships is recorded in CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income.&#160;&#160;For more information, see Note 5 - &#8220;Acquisitions, Divestitures and Investments.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Basis of Presentation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This Annual Report on Form 10-K is a combined report of CH Energy Group and Central Hudson.&#160;&#160;The Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements apply to both CH Energy Group and Central Hudson.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Financial Statements include the accounts of CH Energy Group and its wholly owned subsidiaries, which include Central Hudson and CHEC.&#160;&#160;Operating results of Griffith, CH-Auburn, CH-Greentree, CH Shirley and Lyonsdale are consolidated in the Consolidated Financial Statements of CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;The non-controlling interest shown on CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Financial Statements represents the minority owner&#8217;s proportionate share of the income and equity of Shirley Delaware for 2010 and 2009 and Lyonsdale for 2010, 2009 and 2008 prior to the purchase of the minority owner&#8217;s interest.&#160;&#160;Intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Financial Statements were prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;), which for regulated public utilities, includes specific accounting guidance for regulated operations.&#160;&#160;For additional information regarding regulatory accounting, see Note 2 - &#8220;Regulatory Matters.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Reclassification</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 11, 2009, Griffith divested its operations in certain geographic locations.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group has reported the prior period results of these operations in the discontinued operations section of CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Statement of Income.&#160;&#160;For more information, see Note 5 &#8211; &#8220;Acquisitions, Divestitures and Investments.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Consolidation of Variable Interest Entities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries do not have any interests in special purpose entities and do not have material affiliations with any variable interest entities which were not consolidated.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Use of Estimates</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Preparation of the financial statements in accordance with GAAP includes the use of estimates and assumptions by management that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160;&#160;As with all estimates, actual results may differ from those estimated.&#160;&#160;Expense items most affected by the use of estimates are depreciation and amortization (including amortization of intangible assets), reserves for uncollectible accounts receivable, tax reserves, other operating reserves, unbilled revenues, and pension and other post-retirement benefits.&#160;&#160;Depreciation and amortization is based on estimates of the useful lives and estimated net salvage value of properties (as described in this Note&#160;under the caption &#8220;Depreciation and Amortization&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Amortizable intangible assets include customer relationships related to Griffith, which are amortized based on an assessment of customer attrition as described in Note&#160;6<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>-<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>&#8220;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets.&#8221;</font></div>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Estimates for uncollectible accounts are based on customer accounts receivable aging data as well as consideration of various quantitative and qualitative factors, including special collection issues.&#160;&#160;In the current year, the decrease in the allowance for doubtful accounts reflects the impact of stable energy prices and the improvement in the local unemployment rate, along with enhanced collection efforts.&#160;&#160;The estimates for other operating reserves are based on assessments of future obligations related to injuries and damages and workers compensation claims.&#160;&#160;Unbilled revenues are determined based on the estimated sales for bimonthly accounts that have not been billed by Central Hudson in the current month.&#160;&#160;The estimation methods used in determining these sales are the same methods used for billing customers when actual meter readings cannot be obtained.&#160;&#160;Estimated unbilled revenues are reported as current assets, and include amounts recorded both in revenues and as regulatory liabilities.&#160;&#160;Revenues for 2010, 2009 and 2008 include an estimate for unbilled revenues of $10.1 million, $8.9&#160;million and $8.2&#160;million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Pursuant to regulatory requirements, a portion of unbilled revenue is offset by a regulatory liability and is not included in revenues.&#160;&#160;The portion of unbilled revenues offset by a regulatory liability at December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008 was $6.1 million, $5.2 million and $4.4 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2010, Central Hudson elected to change its tax return methodology for claiming deductions for incidental repair and maintenance expenditures on its utility assets.&#160;&#160;The change accelerates the recognition of the tax deduction from later periods.&#160;&#160;Although the Company believes that its methodology for claiming the deduction is consistent with the Internal Revenue Code and case law, it is unclear whether the Internal Revenue Service will accept the entirety of the deduction claimed.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the Company has recorded a reserve based upon the expected outcome on audit.&#160;&#160;See Note 4 &#8211; &#8220;Income Taxes&#8221; for further discussion of the tax reserve established.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The significant assumptions and estimates used to account for the pension plan and other post-retirement benefit expenses and liabilities are the discount rate, the expected long-term rate of return on the retirement plan and post-retirement plan assets, the rate of compensation increase, the healthcare cost trend rate, mortality assumptions, and the method of amortizing gains and losses.&#160;&#160;For more information of the significant assumptions and estimates, see Note 10 &#8211; &#8220;Post-Employment Benefits.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Estimates are also reflected for certain commitments and contingencies where there is sufficient basis to project a future obligation.&#160;&#160;Disclosures related to these certain commitments and contingencies are included in Note&#160;12 - &#8220;Commitments and Contingencies.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Rates, Revenues, and Cost Adjustment Clauses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s electric and natural gas retail rates are regulated by the New York State Public Service Commission (&#8220;PSC&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Transmission rates, facilities charges, and rates for electricity sold for resale in interstate commerce are regulated by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (&#8220;FERC&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s tariffs for retail electric and natural gas service include purchased electricity and purchased natural gas cost adjustment clauses&#160;by which electric and natural gas rates are adjusted to collect the actual purchased electricity and purchased natural gas costs incurred in providing these services.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective July 1, 2009 and continuing in the 2010 Rate Order, Central Hudson&#8217;s delivery rate structure includes revenue decoupling mechanisms (&#8220;RDMs&#8221;), which provide the ability to record revenues equal to those forecasted in the development of current rates for most of Central Hudson&#8217;s customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenue Recognition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson records revenue on the basis of meters read.&#160;&#160;In addition, Central Hudson records an estimate of unbilled revenue for service rendered to bimonthly customers whose meters are read in the prior month.&#160;&#160;The estimate covers 30 days subsequent to the meter-read date.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, and 2009, the portion of estimated electric unbilled revenues that is unrecognized in accordance with current regulatory agreements were $12.1 million and $10.1 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;The full amount of estimated natural gas unbilled revenues are recognized on the Consolidated Balance Sheet.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As required by the PSC, Central Hudson records gross receipts tax revenues and expenses on a gross income statement presentation basis (i.e., included in both revenue and expenses).&#160;&#160;Sales and use taxes for both Central Hudson and Griffith are accounted for on a net basis (excluded from revenue).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Griffith records revenue when products are delivered to customers or services have been rendered.&#160;&#160;Deferred revenues include unamortized payments from fuel oil burner maintenance and tank service agreements, as well as fees paid by customers for price-protected programs.&#160;&#160;These agreements require a one-time payment from the customer at inception of the agreements.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s deferred revenue balances as of December 31, 2010 and 2009 were $4.7 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;The deferred revenue balance will be recognized in competitive business subsidiaries&#8217; operating revenues over the 12-month term of the respective customer contract.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For Central Hudson and Griffith, payments received from customers who participate in budget billing, whose balance represents the amount paid in excess of deliveries received at December&#160;31, are included in customer advances.&#160;&#160;On an annual basis, each such customer&#8217;s budget billings are reconciled with their actual purchases and the accounts are settled.</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Utility Plant - Central Hudson</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The cost of additions to utility plant and replacements of retired units of property are capitalized at original cost.&#160;&#160;Capitalized costs include labor, materials and supplies, indirect charges for such items as transportation, certain taxes, pension and other employee benefits, and allowances for funds used during construction (&#8220;AFUDC&#8221;), as further discussed below.&#160;&#160;The replacement of minor items of property is included in operating expenses.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The original cost of property, together with removal cost less salvage, is charged to accumulated depreciation at the time the property is retired and removed from service as required by the PSC.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Allowance For Funds Used During Construction</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s regulated utility plant includes AFUDC, which is defined as the net cost of borrowed funds used for construction purposes and a reasonable rate on other funds when so used.&#160;&#160;The concurrent credit for the amount so capitalized is reported in the Consolidated Statement of Income as follows: the portion applicable to borrowed funds is reported as a reduction of interest charges while the portion applicable to other funds (the equity component, a noncash item) is reported as other income.&#160;&#160;The AFUDC rate was 3.00% in 2010, 1.00% in 2009, and 3.00% in 2008.&#160;&#160;The amounts recorded for borrowed funds for the years 2010, 2009, and 2008 are $0.2 million, $0.2 million, and $0.6 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;In 2010, $0.3 million was recorded for the equity component of AFUDC.&#160;&#160;There were no equity components of AFUDC in 2009 or 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Depreciation and Amortization</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The regulated assets of Central Hudson include electric, natural gas, and common assets and are listed under the heading &#8220;Utility Plant&#8221; on Central Hudson&#8217;s and CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;The accumulated depreciation associated with these regulated assets is also reported on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For financial statement purposes, Central Hudson&#8217;s depreciation provisions are computed on the straight-line method using rates based on studies of the estimated useful lives and estimated net salvage values of properties.&#160;&#160;The anticipated costs of removing assets upon retirement are generally provided for over the life of those assets as a component of depreciation expense.&#160;&#160;This depreciation method is consistent with industry practice and the applicable depreciation rates have been approved by the PSC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Current accounting guidance related to asset retirement, precludes the recognition of expected future retirement obligations as a component of depreciation expense or accumulated depreciation.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson, however, is required to use depreciation methods and rates approved by the PSC under regulatory accounting.&#160;&#160;In accordance with current accounting guidance for Regulated Operations, Central Hudson continues to accrue for the future cost of removal for its rate-regulated natural gas and electric utility assets.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson has classified $46.9 million and $47.0&#160;million of net cost of removal as a regulatory liability as of December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson performs depreciation studies periodically and, upon approval by the PSC, adjusts the depreciation rates of its various classes of depreciable property.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s composite rates for depreciation were 2.74% in 2010, 2.75% in 2009, and 2.74% in 2008 of the original average cost of depreciable property.&#160;&#160;The ratio of the amount of accumulated depreciation to the original cost of depreciable property at December&#160;31 was 28.5% in 2010, 28.4% in 2009, and 29.4% in 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For financial statement purposes, depreciation provisions at Griffith and CHEC&#8217;s other subsidiaries are computed on the straight-line method using depreciation rates based on the estimated useful lives of the depreciable property and equipment.&#160;&#160;Expenditures for major renewals and betterments, which extend the useful lives of property and equipment are capitalized.&#160;&#160;Expenditures for maintenances and repairs are charged to expense when incurred.&#160;&#160;Retirements, sales and disposals of assets are recorded by removing the cost and accumulated depreciation from the asset and accumulated depreciation accounts with any resulting gain or loss reflected in earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See Note&#160;6 - &#8220;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets&#8221; for further discussion of amortization of intangibles (other than goodwill).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Research and Development</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is engaged in the conduct and support of research and development (&#8220;R&amp;D&#8221;) activities, which are focused on the improvement of existing energy technologies and the development of new technologies for the delivery and customer use of energy.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s R&amp;D expenditures were $3.1 million in 2010 and $3.9 million in both 2009 and 2008.&#160;&#160;These expenditures were for internal research programs and for contributions to research administered by New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (&#8220;NYSERDA&#8221;), the Electric Power Research Institute, and other industry organizations.&#160;&#160;R&amp;D expenditures are provided for in Central Hudson&#8217;s rates charged to customers for electric and natural gas delivery service, with any differences between R&amp;D expense and the rate allowances deferred for future recovery from or return to customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income Tax</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries file consolidated federal and state income tax returns.&#160;&#160;Income taxes are deferred under the asset and liability method in accordance with current accounting guidance for income taxes, resulting in deferred income taxes for all differences between the financial statement and the tax basis of assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Additional deferred income taxes and offsetting regulatory assets or liabilities are recorded by Central Hudson to recognize that income taxes will be recovered or refunded through future revenues.&#160;&#160;For federal and state income tax purposes, CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries use an accelerated method of depreciation and generally use the shortest life permitted for each class of assets.&#160;&#160;Deferred investment tax credits are amortized over the estimated life of the properties giving rise to the credits.&#160;&#160;For state income tax purposes, Central Hudson uses book depreciation for property placed in service in 1999 or earlier in accordance with transition property rules under Article&#160;9-A of the New York State Tax Law.&#160;&#160;CHEC, Griffith, Shirley Delaware and Lyonsdale file state income tax returns in those states in which they conduct business.&#160;&#160;For more information, see Note&#160;4 - &#8220;Income Tax.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Equity-Based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Product Warranties</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Griffith offers a multi-year warranty on heating system installations and has recorded liabilities for the estimated costs of fulfilling its obligations under these warranties.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s approximate aggregate potential liability for product warranties at both December 31, 2010 and 2009 was $0.1 million.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s liability for these product warranties were determined by accruing the present value of future estimated warranty expense based on the number and type of contracts outstanding and historical costs for these contracts.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Common Stock Dividends</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s ability to pay dividends is affected by the ability of its subsidiaries to pay dividends.&#160;&#160;The Federal Power Act limits the payment of dividends by Central Hudson to its retained earnings.&#160;&#160;More restrictive is the PSC&#8217;s limit on the dividends Central Hudson may pay to CH Energy Group which is 100% of the average annual income available for common stock, calculated on a two-year rolling average basis.&#160;&#160;Based on this calculation as of December 31, 2010, Central Hudson would be able to pay a maximum of $38.5 million in dividends to CH Energy Group without violating the restrictions by the PSC.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s dividend would be reduced to 75% of its average annual income in the event of a downgrade of its senior debt rating below &#8220;BBB+&#8221; by more than one rating agency if the stated reason for the downgrade is related to CH Energy Group or any of Central Hudson&#8217;s affiliates.&#160;&#160;Further restrictions are imposed for any downgrades below this level.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2010, Central Hudson declared and paid dividends of $31.0 million to CH Energy Group.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group&#8217;s other subsidiaries do not have express restrictions on their ability to pay dividends.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 16, 2010, the Board of Directors of CH Energy Group declared a quarterly dividend of $0.54 per share, payable February 1, 2011, to shareholders of record as of January 10, 2011.</font></div>
