<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note2">NOTE 2</a> &#8211; Regulatory Matters</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Effective June 30, 1998 (and amended March 7, 2000), the PSC approved a settlement agreement (the &#8220;Settlement Agreement&#8221;) between Central Hudson, PSC staff and certain other parties.</font><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Settlement Agreement included the following major provisions which survived its expiration date: (i)&#160;certain limitations on ownership of electric generation facilities by Central Hudson and its affiliates in Central Hudson&#8217;s franchise territory; (ii)&#160;standards of conduct in transactions between Central Hudson, CH Energy Group, and any other subsidiaries of CH Energy Group (such as CHEC and Griffith); (iii)&#160;prohibitions against Central Hudson making loans to CH Energy Group or any other subsidiary of CH Energy Group and against Central Hudson guaranteeing debt of CH Energy Group or any other subsidiary of CH Energy Group; (iv)&#160;limitations on the transfer of Central Hudson employees to CH Energy Group or other CH Energy Group subsidiaries; (v) certain dividend payment restrictions on Central Hudson; and (vi) treatment of savings up to the amount of an acquisition&#8217;s or merger&#8217;s premium or costs flowing from a merger with another utility company.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulatory Accounting Policies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulated companies such as Central Hudson apply AFUDC to the cost of construction projects and defer costs and credits on the balance sheet as regulatory assets and liabilities (see the caption &#8220;Summary of Regulatory Assets and Liabilities&#8221; of this Note) when it is probable that those costs and credits will be recoverable through the rate-making process in a period different from when they otherwise would have been reflected in income.&#160;&#160;For Central Hudson, these deferred regulatory assets and liabilities, and the related deferred taxes, are then either eliminated by offset as directed by the PSC or reflected in the Consolidated Statement of Income in the period in which the same amounts are reflected in rates.&#160;&#160;In addition, current accounting practices reflect the regulatory accounting authorized in the most recent settlement agreement or rate order, whichever the case may be.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The significant regulatory assets and liabilities include:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">PSC General and Temporary State Assessment:&#160; </font><font style="FONT-STYLE: normal">In April 2009, the PSC issued an order instituting a new Temporary State Assessment to be collected through utility bills as mandated by NYS. Central Hudson is required to make bi-annual payments of this assessment, in conjunction with its payments of the PSC, General Assessment, and collect the amount from customers in subsequent months. Deferral accounting for both these assessments was authorized in this order.</font></font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><br>
</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">RDM:</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: normal">&#160; The 2009 and 2010 Rate Orders authorized a revenue decoupling mechanism as part of the rate increase, which allows Central Hudson to recognize revenues at the level approved in rates for most of Central Hudson&#8217;s electric customer classes and recognize sales at the approved level per customer in rates for most of Central Hudson&#8217;s natural gas customer classes.</font></font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><br>
</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Storm Costs:&#160; </font><font style="FONT-STYLE: normal">In late February 2010, Central Hudson&#8217;s service territory experienced a significant snow storm event, which disrupted service to approximately 210,000 customers.&#160;&#160;The $19.7 million deferred incremental cost was calculated based on the methodology established in prior approved orders.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson filed a petition with the PSC for approval and recovery on September 23, 2010.&#160;&#160;Management believes that the restoration costs deferred meet the PSC criteria and are probable of future recovery.</font></font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Uncollectible Deferral:</font>&#160;&#160;On June 30, 2010, Central Hudson recorded $2.6 million of incremental electric uncollectible expense for the rate year ended June 30, 2010 and filed a petition with the PSC for approval and recovery on September 23, 2010.&#160;&#160;The amount deferred was calculated based on the methodology established in prior approved orders and Management believes the incremental expense meets the PSC criteria and is probable of future recovery.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Deferred Pension Costs</font>:&#160;&#160;Deferred pension costs recoverable from customers include the following: (A) As discussed further in Note&#160;10 - &#8220;Post-Employment Benefits,&#8221; the amount of deferred pension cost undercollected as of December 31, 2010 and December 31, 2009, includes $137.5 million and $164.6 million, respectively, related to the current accounting guidance related to pensions for recording the funded status.&#160;&#160;(B) The remaining $5.1 million and $4.1&#160;million at December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively, are the cumulative undercollected pension costs in excess of amounts provided in rates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Carrying Charges - Pension Reserve:</font>&#160;&#160;Under the policy of the PSC regarding pension costs, carrying charges are accrued on cash differences between rate allowances and cash contributions to Central Hudson&#8217;s defined benefit pension plan.&#160;&#160;For further discussion regarding this plan, see Note&#160;10 - &#8220;Post-Employment Benefits.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Deferred Medicare Subsidy Taxes:</font>&#160; The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act signed into law on March 23, 2010, contains a provision which changes the tax treatment related to the Retiree Drug Subsidy benefit under the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act (under Medicare Part D).&#160;&#160;This change reduces the employer's deduction for the costs of health care for retirees by the amount of Retiree Drug Subsidy payments received.&#160;&#160;As a result, the deductible temporary difference and any related deferred tax asset associated with the benefit plan were reduced.&#160;&#160;Under the PSC policy regarding Medicare Act Effects, cost savings and income tax effects related to the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act are deferred for future recovery from or refund to customers resulting in a new regulatory asset of $6.7 million for the reduction in deferred taxes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Residual Natural Gas Deferred Balances</font>:&#160;&#160;As a result of the 2006, 2009 and 2010 Rate Orders, certain gas regulatory assets and liabilities were identified for offset and reduced by a depreciation reserve adjustment, resulting in an increase to the net regulatory asset.&#160; The remaining balance&#160;is being amortized over a four-year period which began&#160;July 1, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Income Taxes Recoverable</font>:&#160; Regulatory asset balance established to offset deferred tax liabilities because&#160;it is probable that they will be recoverable from customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Excess Electric Depreciation Reserve (&#8220;EDR&#8221;):</font>&#160;&#160;Under the 2009 Rate Order, this balance was to be used for authorized rate moderation which totaled $25.5 million from July 1, 2009 through June 30, 2010.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the 2010 Rate Order, $6.8 million was used for authorized rate moderation from July 1, 2010 through December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;The current portion of the EDR as of December 31, 2010 represents the amount estimated to be used for rate moderation in the next twelve months related to the Electric Bill Credit and Incremental Finance Charges.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Income Taxes Refundable:</font>&#160;&#160;Regulatory liability balances established to offset deferred tax assets because it is probable that the related balances will be refundable to customers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Customer Benefit Fund:&#160; </font>The 2010 Order prescribes the use of the residual balance to fund economic development.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">Carrying Charges - OPEB Reserve:</font>&#160;&#160;Under the policy of the PSC regarding OPEB costs, carrying charges are accrued on cash differences between rate allowances and cash contributions to Central Hudson&#8217;s OPEB plan.&#160;&#160;For further discussion regarding this plan, see Note&#160;10 - &#8220;Post-Employment Benefits.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note4">NOTE 4</a> &#8211; Income Tax</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries file a consolidated Federal and New York State income tax return.&#160;&#160;CHEC, Griffith, Shirley Delaware and Lyonsdale also file state income tax returns in those states in which they conduct business.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In September of 2010, Central Hudson filed a request with the Internal Revenue Service (&#8220;IRS&#8221;) to change the company&#8217;s tax accounting method related to costs to repair and maintain utility assets.&#160;&#160;The change was effective for the tax year ending December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;This change allows Central Hudson to take a current tax deduction for a significant amount of expenditure that was previously capitalized for tax purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This change resulted in federal and state net operating income tax losses (&#8220;NOL&#8221;).&#160;&#160;For Federal tax purposes, CH Energy Group has elected to carry back the NOL, which resulted in tax refunds for the tax years 2004 through 2008 and carry forward the 2010 NOL to future periods.&#160;&#160;For NYS tax purposes, the 2009 and 2010 NOL will be carried forward to future periods.&#160;&#160;NOL carry forwards will expire in 20 years if not otherwise utilized.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group believes future taxable income will more likely than not be sufficient to utilize substantially all its tax carryforwards prior to their expiration.&#160;&#160;Future tax benefits resulting from this change are included within &#8220;Accumulated Deferred Income Tax&#8221; on the CH Energy Group Consolidated Balance Sheet and the Central Hudson Balance Sheet.&#160;&#160;NOL carryforwards are summarized as follows (In Thousands):</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The final regulations that will clarify what qualifies as deductible repair and maintenance expenditures for prospective tax years are still being formulated.&#160;&#160;Due to uncertainty under current law, Central Hudson has established reserves against a portion of the tax benefits claimed.&#160;&#160;For Federal tax purposes, $8.3 million has been reserved against federal income tax refunds received as a result of 2009 NOL carried back to prior years and $1.6 million has been reserved against the 2010 NOL Deferred Tax Asset carried forward.&#160;&#160;For NYS tax purposes, an additional $1.6 million has been reserved against the 2009 and 2010 NOL Deferred Tax Asset carry forward.&#160;&#160;These reserves are shown as &#8220;Tax Reserve&#8221; under the Deferred Credits and Other Liabilities section of the CH Energy Group Consolidated Balance Sheet and the Central Hudson Balance Sheet.&#160;&#160;Interest is being accrued on this reserve at the applicable IRS rate and is included in &#8220;Accrued Interest&#8221; under current liabilities on the CH Energy Group Consolidated Balance Sheet and the Central Hudson Balance Sheet and included in &#8220;Interest on regulatory liabilities and other interest&#8221; under Interest Charges on the CH Energy Group Consolidated Statement of Income and the Central Hudson Statement of Income.&#160;&#160;No penalties have been recorded related to this uncertain tax position.&#160;&#160;If CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries incur any penalties on underpayment of taxes, the amounts would be included in &#8220;Other&#8221; under the Current Liabilities section of the Balance Sheets and &#8220;Other-net&#8221; under the Other Income and Deductions section of the Statements of Income.</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The significant decrease in current income tax expense in 2010 as opposed to 2009 is driven primarily by the effect of the tax accounting change.&#160;&#160;The one-time deduction is a temporary difference between book and tax expense and requires normalization, resulting in an offsetting deferred tax expense, which is the primary driver of the significant increase in deferred income tax expense in 2010 as compared to 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The difference in the effective tax rate for 2010 is also impacted by a one-time reclassification of funded deferred taxes to a regulatory liability, resulting in a reduction to the tax provision of $2.3 million.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 1, 2010, CHEC purchased the remaining 25% ownership stake in Lyonsdale and is now the 100% owner.&#160;&#160;Lyonsdale owns and operates a 19-megawatt, wood-fired, biomass electric generating plant located in Lyonsdale, New York, which began operation in 1992.&#160;&#160;The energy and capacity of the plant is being sold at a fixed price to an investment grade rated counterparty pursuant to a contract beginning May 1, 2006 and ending December 31, 2014.&#160;&#160;Lyonsdale received $1.2 million of production tax credits in 2009.&#160;&#160;Beginning January 1, 2010, Lyonsdale was no longer eligible to receive production tax credits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the third quarter of 2009, management stopped accruing interest income on the subordinated debt in Cornhusker Holdings in response to the continuation of lower than expected margins.&#160;&#160;During the third quarter of 2010, CHEC recorded a reserve for 100% of its notes and accrued interest and recorded a full impairment of its equity investment in Cornhusker Holdings in response to a change in its expectations regarding Cornhusker Holdings&#8217; ability to service CHEC&#8217;s subordinated debt and pay dividends on equity.&#160;&#160;This change in CHEC&#8217;s expectations during the third quarter was the result of the confluence of various negative trends, including (1) a lower-than-expected level of increased output from the expansion that was completed at the end of 2009 under which CEL took on additional debt that is senior to CHEC&#8217;s debt; (2) continued lower-than-expected margins; and (3) a change in the historical relationship between corn and distillers grains prices at the site that began in the first quarter of 2010.&#160;&#160;The amount of the reserve and impairment charge recorded during the third quarter of 2010 was $11.4 million.&#160; See Note 15 &#8220;Other Fair Value Measurements&#8221; for further discussion of the fair value of the Note Receivable which supports the reserve.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During 2009, CH Shirley, a wholly owned subsidiary of CHEC, agreed to invest approximately $50 million for a 90% controlling interest in a 20-megawatt wind farm facility in Wisconsin.&#160;&#160;This project carries a 20-year power purchase agreement contract at pre-determined electric prices with Wisconsin Public Service Corporation (&#8220;WPSC&#8221;) for the electric output of the wind farm&#8217;s eight wind turbines. The project achieved its commercial operation date under the power purchase agreement on December 4, 2010 and has been selling power to WPSC.&#160;&#160;Construction on this project is nearly complete and it is currently undergoing final testing prior to final acceptance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the fourth quarter of 2010, Management completed an update to its strategic plan, which included a decision to discontinue business development efforts in renewable energy and evaluate the market to potentially divest existing renewable energy investments in a manner that maximizes shareholder value.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group has evaluated CHEC&#8217;s current renewable energy investments and has initiated plans to actively market Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind.&#160;&#160;Management will continue to evaluate the market for the remaining investments in 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Based on the change in the strategy and the marketing efforts related to CHEC&#8217;s Lyonsdale and Shirley Wind investments that began late in the fourth quarter, Management believes it is more likely than not that the long-lived assets of these investments will be sold before the end of their previously estimated useful lives.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, Management performed a test to evaluate whether the carrying amount of these assets exceeds the expected undiscounted cash flow from these assets over their estimated remaining useful lives and whether the carrying amount exceeds the estimated fair value of these assets, which would require the recognition of impairment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For Lyonsdale, Management performed the test using bids received from several parties in early&#160;2011.&#160;&#160;Management believes these proposals represent a market participant&#8217;s fair value of the investment.&#160;&#160;The current proposals indicate it is unlikely that CHEC will receive book value under such sale.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, Management recorded a pre-tax impairment of $2.1 million ($1.3 million after-tax impact on earnings) as of December 31, 2010,&#160;based on the amount by which the&#160;carrying amount exceeded the fair value of these assets.&#160;&#160;Management cannot predict the final outcome of the sale process.&#160;&#160;For further discussions relating to the estimated Fair Value of Lyonsdale assets, see Note 15 &#8211; &#8220;Other Fair Value Measurements&#8221; of this 10-K Annual Report.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note6">NOTE 6</a> &#8211; Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Goodwill, customer relationships, trademarks and covenants not to compete associated with acquisitions are included in intangible assets.&#160;&#160;Goodwill represents the excess of cost over the fair value of the net tangible and identifiable intangible assets of businesses acquired as of the date of acquisition.&#160;&#160;The balances reflected on CH Energy Group&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheet at December 31, 2010 and 2009, for &#8220;Goodwill&#8221; and &#8220;Other intangible assets - net&#8221; relate to Griffith.&#160;&#160;In accordance with current accounting guidance related to goodwill and other intangible assets, goodwill and other intangible assets that have indefinite useful lives are no longer amortized, but instead are periodically reviewed for impairment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Griffith tests goodwill for impairment annually in the fourth quarter. Griffith would retest goodwill between annual tests and test intangible assets if an event should occur or circumstances arise that would more likely than not reduce the fair value below its carrying amount.&#160;&#160;No impairment existed for any of the periods presented.&#160;&#160;At the time of the 2010 annual impairment test, fair value of Griffith exceeded its carrying value by approximately $34.2 million.&#160;&#160;Fair value of the reporting unit is estimated using a weighted average of the discounted cash flow and market approach methodologies.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As a result of the divestiture in December 2009 discussed in Note 5 - &#8220;Acquisitions, Divestitures and Investments,&#8221; Griffith reduced its 2009 goodwill by approximately $10 million in addition to the goodwill recorded when the divested assets were purchased.&#160;&#160;This additional reduction was recorded in accordance with current accounting guidance related to goodwill, which requires an allocation of goodwill based on the fair values of the divested region and the portion of the business retained.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s and Central Hudson&#8217;s credit facilities require compliance with certain restrictive covenants, including maintaining a ratio of total consolidated debt to total consolidated capitalization of no more than 0.65 to 1.00.&#160;&#160;Currently, both CH Energy Group and Central Hudson are in compliance with all of their respective debt covenants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the event of a liquidation of Central Hudson, the holders of the Cumulative Preferred Stock are entitled to receive the redemption price (in the case of a voluntary liquidation) or the par value (in the case of an involuntary liquidation) plus, in either case, accrued dividends.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Repurchase Program</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On July&#160;25, 2002, the Board of Directors of CH Energy Group authorized a Common Stock Repurchase Program (&#8220;Repurchase Program&#8221;) to repurchase up to 4&#160;million shares, or approximately 25% of its outstanding Common Stock, over the </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">five-year period ending July 31, 2007.&#160;&#160;Effective July 31, 2007, the Board of Directors of CH Energy Group extended and amended the Repurchase Program.&#160;&#160;As amended, the Repurchase Program authorizes the repurchase of up to 2 million shares (excluding shares purchased before July 31, 2007) or approximately 13% of the Company's outstanding common stock, from time to time, over the five-year period ending July 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2010, CH Energy Group had purchased 29,562 shares under the Repurchase Program.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group intends to purchase additional shares under the plan during 2011.&#160;&#160;No shares were repurchased under the Repurchase Program during the years ended December 31, 2009 and 2008.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group reserves the right to modify, suspend, renew, or terminate the Repurchase Program at any time without notice.</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Long-Term Debt Maturities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">See Note 15 - &#8220;Fair Value Measurements&#8221; for a schedule of long-term debt maturing or to be redeemed during the next five years and thereafter.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On September 22, 2009, the PSC authorized Central Hudson to issue up to $250 million of long-term debt through December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;The Order authorizes Central Hudson to issue and sell $250 million of long-term debt to finance its construction expenditures, refund maturing long-term debt, and potentially refinance its 1999 NYSERDA Bonds, Series B, C and D.&#160;&#160;On November 20, 2009, Central Hudson registered a new series of notes, Series G, pursuant to the authority granted by the PSC.&#160;&#160;An amended registration statement was filed on December 23, 2009 and the registration of the Series G notes became effective on January 6, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On September 21, 2010, Central Hudson entered into a Note Purchase Agreement to issue and sell, in a private placement exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, $40 million of senior unsecured notes in two series.&#160;&#160;Series A bear interest at the rate of 4.30% per annum on a principal amount of $16 million and mature on September 21, 2020.&#160;&#160;Series B bear interest at the rate of 5.64% per annum on a principal amount of $24 million and mature on September 21, 2040.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson used a portion of the proceeds from the sale of the notes for refunding maturing long term debt and retained the rest for general corporate purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NYSERDA</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On December 7, 2010, Central Hudson issued $82.15 million of unsecured Medium Term Notes registered under Series G in three maturities.&#160;&#160;The first maturity bears interest at the rate of 2.756% per annum on a principal amount of $8 million and matures on April 1, 2016.&#160;&#160;The second maturity bears interest at the rate of 4.15% per annum on a principal amount of $44.15 million and matures on April 1, 2021.&#160;&#160;The third maturity bears interest at the rate of 5.716% per annum on a principal amount of $30 million and matures on April 1, 2041.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson used the proceeds from the sale of the notes for refunding its 1999 NYSERDA Bonds Series C and Series D of $41.15 million and $41.0 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson has retired these Series C and Series D NYSERDA Bonds and no notes are outstanding in these two Series.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s Series B NYSERDA Bonds total $33.7 million at December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;These bonds are tax-exempt multi-modal bonds that are currently in a variable rate mode.&#160;&#160;In its Orders, the PSC has authorized deferral accounting treatment for variations in the interest costs from these bonds.&#160;&#160;As such, variations between the actual interest rates on these bonds and the interest rate included in the current delivery rate structure for these bonds are deferred for future recovery from or refund to customers.&#160; As a result, variations in interest rates do not have any impact on earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To mitigate the potential cash flow impact of unexpected increases in short-term interest rates, Central Hudson purchases interest rate caps based on an index of short-term tax-exempt debt.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson&#8217;s one year rate caps for the bond series, set at 3.0%, expired on March 31, 2010 and were replaced with three new rate caps.&#160;&#160;Effective April 1, 2010, the new rate caps are set at 5.0%.&#160;&#160;Two of the rate caps were one-year in length with notional amounts that were aligned to the Series C and Series D NYSERDA Bonds and are no longer outstanding.&#160;&#160;These two rate caps will expire on April 1, 2011.&#160;&#160;The third rate cap is two years in length with a notional amount aligned with Series B and will expire on April 1, 2012.&#160;&#160;The caps are based on the monthly weighted average of an index of tax-exempt variable rate debt, multiplied by 175%.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson would receive a payout if the adjusted index exceeds 5.0% for a given month.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is currently evaluating what actions, if any, it may take in the future in connection with its Series B NYSERDA Bonds.&#160;&#160;Potential actions may include converting the debt to another interest rate mode or refinancing with taxable bonds.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Debt Expense</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Expenses incurred in connection with CH Energy Group&#8217;s or Central Hudson&#8217;s debt issuance and any discount or premium on debt are deferred and amortized over the lives of the related issues.&#160;&#160;Expenses incurred and unamortized costs written off on debt redemptions prior to maturity have been deferred and are usually amortized over the shorter of the remaining lives of the related extinguished issues or the new issues, as directed by the PSC.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Debt Covenants</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s $50 million of privately placed notes require compliance with certain restrictive covenants including maintaining a ratio of total consolidated debt to total consolidated capitalization of no more than 0.65 to 1.00 and not permitting certain debt, other than the privately placed notes, associated with the unregulated operations of CH Energy Group to exceed 10% of total consolidated assets.&#160;&#160;Currently, CH Energy Group is in compliance with all of these debt covenants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note10">NOTE 10</a> &#8211; Post-Employment Benefits</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Pension Benefits</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson has a non-contributory Retirement Income Plan (&#8220;Retirement Plan&#8221;) covering substantially all of its employees hired before January 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;The Retirement Plan is a defined benefit plan, which provides pension benefits based on an employee&#8217;s compensation and years of service.&#160;&#160;In 2007, Central Hudson amended the Retirement Plan to eliminate these benefits for managerial, professional, and supervisory employees hired on or after January 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;The Retirement Plan for unionized employees was similarly amended for all employees hired on or after May 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;The Retirement Plan&#8217;s assets are held in a trust fund (&#8220;Trust Fund&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Central Hudson has provided periodic updates to the benefit formulas stated in the Retirement Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Decisions to fund Central Hudson&#8217;s Retirement Plan are based on several factors, including, but not limited to, corporate resources, projected investment returns, actual investment returns, inflation, the value of plan assets relative to plan liabilities, regulatory considerations, interest rate assumptions and the Pension Protection Act of 2006 (&#8220;PPA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Based on the funding requirements of the PPA, Central Hudson plans to make contributions that maintain the target funded percentage at 80% or higher.&#160;&#160;Contributions to the Retirement Plan during the years ended December 31, 2010 and 2009 were $64.2 million and $22.6 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The fair value of the plan assets have increased by approximately $82.7 million in 2010, reflecting significant contributions and asset returns that were partially offset by benefit payments and administrative expenses.&#160;&#160;Plan liabilities, however, increased by approximately $32.9 million, reflecting a decline in the plan discount rate.&#160;&#160;The net impact was a reduction in the unfunded liability of approximately $49.8 million.&#160;&#160;Contributions for 2011 are expected to be approximately $32 million.&#160;&#160;As noted above, actual contributions could vary significantly based upon a range of factors that Central Hudson considers in its funding decisions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Gains or losses and prior service costs or credits that arise during the period but that are not recognized as components of net periodic pension cost would typically be recognized as a component of other comprehensive income, net of tax.&#160;&#160;However, Central Hudson has PSC approval to record regulatory assets rather than adjusting comprehensive income to offset the additional liability.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The valuation of the current and prior year PBO was determined as of the measurement date of December 31, 2010 and 2009, using discount rates of 5.3% for 2010 and 5.7% for 2009 (as determined using the Citigroup Pension Discount Curve reflecting projected pension cash flows).&#160;&#160;Central Hudson accounts for pension activity in accordance with PSC-prescribed provisions, which among other things, require a ten-year amortization of actuarial gains and losses.&#160;&#160;Declines in the market value of the Trust Fund&#8217;s investment portfolio, which occurred from 2000 through 2002, and a reduction in the discount rate during that period used to determine the benefit obligation for pensions have resulted in a significant increase in pension costs since 2001.&#160;&#160;Similarly, declines in the market value of the Trust Fund&#8217;s investment portfolio in 2008 resulted in increased future pension costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 2010 Rate Order includes an increase in the rate allowance for pension and OPEB expense which more closely approximates the recent cost of providing these benefits.&#160;&#160;Authorization remains in effect for the deferral of any differences between rate allowances and actual costs under the 1993 PSC Policy to counteract the volatility of these costs.&#160;&#160;The 2010 Rate Order again authorized Central Hudson to offset significant deferred balances for pension and OPEB expense for the electric department with available deferred credit balances due to customers.&#160;&#160;The 2010 Rate Order also authorized the continuation of the amortization of natural gas department deferred pension and OPEB costs.&#160;&#160;The accumulated deferred balance of these costs at June 30, 2010 is being recovered via a four-year amortization that began July 1, 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Retirement Plan Estimates of Long-Term Rates of Return</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The expected long-term rate of return on Retirement Plan assets is 7.75%, net of investment expense.&#160;&#160;In determining the expected long-term rate of return on these assets, Central Hudson considered the current level of expected returns on risk-free investments (primarily United States government bonds), the historical level of risk premiums associated with other asset classes, and the expectations of future returns over a 20-year time horizon on each asset class, based on the views of leading financial advisors and economists.&#160;&#160;The expected return for each asset class was then weighted based on the Retirement Plan&#8217;s target asset allocation.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson monitors actual performance against target asset allocations and adjusts actual allocations and targets in accordance with the Retirement Plan strategy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Retirement Plan Policy and Strategy</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s Retirement Plan investment policy seeks to achieve long-term growth and income to match the long-term nature of its funding obligations.&#160;&#160;During the first quarter of 2010, Management began a transition to a long-duration investment (&#8220;LDI&#8221;) strategy for its pension plan assets.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s objective is to minimize the plan&#8217;s funded status volatility and the level of contributions by more closely aligning the characteristics of plan assets with liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other Post-Retirement Benefits</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson provides certain health care and life insurance benefits for retired employees through its post-retirement benefit plans.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of Central Hudson&#8217;s unionized employees and managerial, professional and supervisory employees (&#8220;non-union&#8221;) hired prior to January 1, 2008, may become eligible for these benefits if they reach retirement age while employed by Central Hudson.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson amended its OPEB programs for existing non-union and certain retired employees effective January 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;Benefit plans for non-union active employees were similarly amended.&#160;&#160;Programs were also amended to eliminate post-retirement benefits for non-union employees hired on or after January 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;In order to reduce the total costs of these benefits, plan changes were negotiated with the IBEW Local 320 for unionized employees and certain retired employees effective May 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;Plans were also amended to eliminate post-retirement benefits for union employees hired on or after May 1, 2008.&#160;&#160;Benefits for retirees and active employees are provided through insurance companies whose premiums are based on the benefits paid during the year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The significant assumptions used to account for these benefits are the discount rate, the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets and the health care cost trend rate.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson selects the discount rate using the C</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">itigroup Pension Discount Curve reflecting projected cash flows.&#160;&#160;The estimates of long-term rates of return and the investment policy and strategy for these plan assets are similar to those used for pension benefits previously discussed in this Note.&#160;&#160;The estimates of health care cost trend rates are based on a review of actual recent trends and projected future trends.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson fully recovers its net periodic post-retirement benefit costs in accordance with the 1993 PSC Policy.&#160;&#160;Under these guidelines, the difference between the amounts of post-retirement benefits recoverable in rates and the amounts of post-retirement benefits determined by an actuarial consultant in accordance with current accounting guidance related to other post employment benefits is deferred as either a regulatory asset or a regulatory liability, as appropriate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The effect of the Medicare Act of 2003 was reflected in 2010 and 2009, assuming that Central Hudson will continue to provide a prescription drug benefit to retirees that are at least actuarially equivalent to Medicare Act of 2003 and that Central Hudson will receive the federal subsidy. The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act signed into law on March 23, 2010, contains a provision which changes the tax treatment related to the Retiree Drug Subsidy benefit under the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act (under Medicare Part D).&#160; This change reduces the employer's deduction for the costs of health care for retirees by the amount of Retiree Drug Subsidy payments received.&#160; As a result, the deductible temporary difference and any related deferred tax asset associated with the benefit plan were reduced.&#160; Under the PSC policy regarding Medicare Act Effects, cost savings and income tax effects related to the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement and Modernization Act are deferred for future recovery from or refund to customers.&#160; See Note 2 &#8211; &#8220;Regulatory Matters&#8221; for further information.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson&#8217;s liability (i.e. the under-funded status) for OPEB at December 31, 2010, was $45.4 million and at December 31, 2009, was $46.2 million, including recognition for the difference between the Accumulated Benefit Obligation (&#8220;ABO&#8221;) and the market value of other post-retirement assets.&#160;&#160;The change to the liability for the difference between the ABO and the market value of other post-retirement assets at December 31, 2010 and 2009 was a decrease of $7.9 million and $1.2 million, respectively, and was offset by recording a regulatory asset in accordance with the 1993 PSC Policy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson and Griffith each participate in a 401(k) retirement plan for their employees.&#160;&#160;Griffith also provides a discretionary profit-sharing benefit for their employees.&#160;&#160;The 401(k) plans provide for employee tax-deferred salary deductions for participating employees and their respective employer matches contributions made by participating employees.&#160;&#160;The matching benefit varies by employer and employee group.&#160;&#160;For Central Hudson, the cost of its matching contributions was $2.0 million for 2010, $1.8 million for 2009, and $1.7 million for 2008.&#160;&#160;For Griffith, the cost of its matching contributions was $0.5 million for 2010 and $0.9 million for both 2009 and 2008.&#160;&#160;Profit-sharing contributions made by Griffith were $0.4 million for 2010 and $0.6 million for both 2009 and 2008, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">OPEB Estimates of Long-Term Rates of Return</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The expected long-term rate of return on OPEB assets is 8.0%, net of investment expense.&#160;&#160;In determining the expected long-term rate of return on these assets, Central Hudson considered the current level of expected returns on risk-free investments, the historical level of risk premiums associated with other asset classes, and the expectations of future returns over a 20-year time horizon on each asset class, based on the views of leading financial advisors and economists.&#160;&#160;The expected return for each asset class was then weighted based on the respective Plans&#8217; target asset allocation.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson monitors actual performance against target asset allocations and adjusts actual allocations and targets as deemed appropriate in accordance with the Plan&#8217;s strategy.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">OPEB Policy and Strategy</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson currently funds its union OPEB obligations through a voluntary employee&#8217;s beneficiary association (&#8220;VEBA&#8221;), which is a form of trust fund. Central Hudson&#8217;s VEBA investment policy seeks to achieve a rate of return for each VEBA over the long term that contributes to meeting each VEBA&#8217;s current and future obligations, including interest and benefit payment obligations.&#160;&#160;The policy also seeks to earn long-term returns from capital appreciation and current income that at least keep pace with inflation over the long term.&#160;&#160;However, there are no assurances that the OPEB Plan&#8217;s return objectives will be achieved.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note11">NOTE 11</a> &#8211; Equity-Based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group&#8217;s Long-Term Performance-Based Incentive Plan (&#8220;2000 Plan&#8221;), adopted in 2000 and amended in 2001 and 2003, reserves 500,000 shares of CH Energy Group&#8217;s Common Stock for awards to be granted under the 2000 Plan.&#160;&#160;The 2000 Plan was amended in the third quarter of 2003.&#160;&#160;The amendment allows executives to defer receipt of performance shares and performance units in accordance with the terms of CH Energy Group&#8217;s Directors and Executives Deferred Compensation Plan.&#160;&#160;Also, an amendment to the previously effective Stock Plan for Outside Directors provided for shares of stock previously accrued for retired Directors to be paid in the form of cash and provides that active Directors could elect to transfer previously accrued shares payable to them to CH Energy Group&#8217;s Directors and Executives Deferred Compensation Plan.&#160;&#160;In addition, the amendment froze future participation and future accruals under the 2000 Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In 2006, CH Energy Group adopted a Long-Term Equity Incentive Plan (&#8220;2006 Plan&#8221;) to replace the 2000 Plan.&#160;&#160;The 2006 Plan was approved by CH Energy Group&#8217;s shareholders on April 25, 2006.&#160;&#160;The 2000 Plan has been terminated, with no new awards to be granted under such plan.&#160;&#160;Outstanding stock option awards granted under the 2000 Plan continue in accordance with their terms and the provisions of the 2000 Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The 2006 Plan reserves up to a maximum of 300,000 shares of CH Energy Group&#8217;s Common Stock for awards to be granted under the 2006 Plan.&#160;&#160;Awards may consist of stock option rights, stock appreciation rights, performance shares, performance units, restricted shares, restricted stock units, and other awards that CH Energy Group&#8217;s Compensation Committee of its Board of Directors (&#8220;Compensation Committee&#8221;) may authorize.&#160;&#160;The Compensation Committee may also, from time-to-time and upon such terms and conditions as it may determine, authorize the granting to non-employee Directors of stock option rights, stock appreciation rights, restricted shares, and restricted stock units.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In addition to the aggregate limit in the awards described above, the 2006 Plan imposes various sub-limits on the number of shares of CH Energy Group&#8217;s Common Stock that may be issued or transferred under the 2006 Plan.&#160;&#160;The aggregate number of shares of Common Stock actually issued or transferred by CH Energy Group upon the exercise of incentive stock options shall not exceed 300,000 shares.&#160;&#160;No participant may be granted stock option rights and stock appreciation rights, in aggregate, for more than 15,000 shares of Common Stock during any calendar year.&#160;&#160;No participant in any calendar year may receive an award of performance shares or restricted shares that specify management objectives, in the aggregate, for more than 20,000 shares of Common Stock, or performance units having an aggregate maximum value as of their respective date of grant in excess of $1 million.&#160;&#160;The number of shares of Common Stock issued as stock appreciation rights, restricted shares, and restricted stock units (after taking forfeitures into account) may not exceed, in the aggregate, 100,000 shares of common stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other considerations in the determination of fair value for performance shares included the grant price for each individual grant, estimated forfeitures, and historical percentile performance rank.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commencing in 2009, CH Energy Group ceased using a binomial model.&#160;&#160;The fair value of performance shares is currently determined based on the shares' current market value at the end of each reporting period, estimated forfeitures for each grant, and expected payout based on Management's best estimate including analysis of historical performance in accordance with the defined metrics of each grant.</font></div>

<div>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Compensation expense for performance shares is recognized over the three year performance period based on the fair value of the awards at the end of each reporting period and the time elapsed within each grant's performance period.&#160;&#160;Compensation expense for restricted shares and stock options is recognized over the defined vesting periods based on the grant date fair value of the awards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Phantom Shares</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group provides equity compensation for its non-employee Directors.&#160;&#160;The equity component of annual compensation for each non-employee Director is fixed at a number of phantom shares of CH Energy Group Common Stock.&#160;&#160;These phantom shares are deferred until the Director&#8217;s termination of service.&#160;&#160;Effective January 1, 2008, CH Energy Group adopted new director stock ownership guidelines, which require each Director to accumulate within 5 years, and to hold during his or her service on the Board, at least 6,000 shares of CH Energy Group&#8217;s Common Stock (which may be in the form of phantom shares).&#160;&#160;This amendment to the plan provides that if a Director satisfies this required level of stock ownership, he or she will receive the cash value of equity compensation in lieu of additional phantom shares.&#160;&#160;This value will either be paid in cash or deferred under CH Energy Group&#8217;s Directors and Executives Deferred Compensation Plan, at the election of the Director.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Through June 30, 2008, the annual equity compensation for each non-employee Director was the equivalent of $55,000.&#160;&#160;Effective July 1, 2008, this compensation was increased to $65,000 per year.&#160;&#160;Total equity compensation expense to non-employee Directors recognized by CH Energy Group was $0.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2010 and 2009 and $0.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">For additional discussion regarding the dilutive effects of equity-based compensation, see Note&#160;1 - &#8220;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; under the caption &#8220;Earnings Per Share.&#8221;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Note12">NOTE 12</a> &#8211; Commitments and Contingencies</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Electricity Purchase Commitments</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson is obligated to supply electricity to its retail electric customers.&#160;&#160;Under the Settlement Agreement, Central Hudson's retail customers may elect to procure electricity from third-party suppliers or may continue to rely on Central Hudson.&#160;&#160;As part of its efforts to supply customers who continue to rely on Central Hudson for their energy supply, Central Hudson entered into an agreement with Constellation to purchase capacity and energy, comprising approximately 9% of the output of Unit No. 2 of the Nine Mile Point Nuclear Generating Station (&#8221;Nine Mile 2 Plant&#8221;) at negotiated prices during the ten-year period beginning on November 7<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">, </font>2001 and ending November 30, 2011. The agreement is "unit-contingent'' in that Constellation is only required to supply electricity if the Nine Mile 2 Plant is operating.&#160;&#160;Following the expiration of this purchase agreement, a revenue sharing agreement with Constellation will begin, which will provide Central Hudson with a hedge against electricity price increases and could provide additional future revenue for Central Hudson through 2021.&#160;&#160;This revenue, if any, will accrue to the benefit of Central Hudson&#8217;s customers.&#160;&#160;In the Constellation agreements, electricity is purchased at defined prices that escalate over the life of the contract.&#160;&#160;The capacity and energy supplied under the agreement with Constellation in 2010 was sufficient to supply approximately 13% of Central Hudson&#8217;s total system requirements and cost approximately $25.9 million.&#160;&#160;For the years 2009 and 2008, the energy supplied under this agreement cost approximately $27.9 million and $25.2 million, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On March 6, 2007<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">, </font>Central Hudson entered into an agreement with Entergy Nuclear&#160;Power Marketing, LLC&#160;to purchase electricity (but not capacity) on a unit-contingent basis at defined prices from January 1, 2008 through December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;On an annual basis, the electricity purchased through the Entergy contract represents approximately 23% of Central Hudson&#8217;s full-service customer requirements and for the year ended December 31, 2010 energy supplied under this agreement cost approximately $56.1 million.&#160;&#160;For the twelve months ended December 31, 2009 and 2008, the energy supplied under this agreement cost approximately $55.3 million and $57.5 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;On June 30, 2010<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>and September 9, 2010,<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>Central Hudson entered into additional agreements with Entergy Nuclear Power Marketing, LLC to purchase electricity (but not capacity) on a unit-contingent basis at defined prices from January 1, 2011 through December 31, 2013.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the event the above noted counterparty is unable to fulfill its commitment to deliver under the terms of the agreements, Central Hudson would obtain the supply from the NYISO market, and under Central Hudson&#8217;s current ratemaking treatment, recover the full cost from customers.&#160;&#160;As such, there would be no impact on earnings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson must also acquire sufficient peak load capacity to meet the peak load requirements of its full service customers.&#160;&#160;This capacity is made up of its own generating capacity, contracts with capacity providers, and purchases from the NYISO capacity market.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating Leases</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries have entered into agreements with various companies which provide products and services to be used in their normal operations.&#160;&#160;These agreements include operating leases for the use of data processing and office equipment, vehicles, office space, and bulk petroleum storage locations.&#160;&#160;The provisions of these leases generally provide for renewal options and some contain escalation clauses.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Operating lease rental payment amounts charged to expense by CH Energy Group and its subsidiaries were $2.7 million in 2010, $2.8 million in 2009, and $3.4 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;Included in 2008 amounts are payments for contingent rentals of $0.6 million, which are operating lease agreements that contain provisions for a change in lease payments subsequent to the inception of the lease.&#160;&#160;CH Energy Group did not have any payments for contingent rentals in 2010 and in 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Operating lease rental payment amounts charged to expense by Central Hudson were $1.7 million in 2010, $1.5 million in 2009, and $2.1 million in 2008.&#160;&#160;Included in 2008 amounts are payments for contingent rentals of $0.6 million.&#160;&#160;Central Hudson did not have any payments for contingent rentals in 2010 or 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Future minimum lease payments excluding executory costs, such as property taxes and insurance, are included in the following table of Other Commitments.&#160;&#160;All leases are non-cancelable, and rent expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the minimum lease term.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Central Hudson</font></div>

<div>

<td>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Air</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
